text:
📰 Article:

I genuinely cannot believe I'm writing this about the sitting Premier of Manitoba, and not because Wab Kinew criticized Donald Trump, wants the Epstein files released, or thinks Trump's foreign policy is a flaming catastrophe. Fill your boots. None of that is particularly remarkable.

I'm writing this because I've now watched the Premier of Manitoba repeatedly take his own suspicions about Trump, Epstein and the Iran war and present them publicly with increasing certainty, without producing the evidence that would justify that certainty. Somewhere between “this might explain it” and “this is why it happened,” speculation quietly became fact simply because Wab Kinew started speaking as though it were.

It isn't.

In early March of this year, while discussing the “why” of the war with Iran with reporters, Kinew offered the Epstein files as “as good of a reason as anyone else can figure out.”

Stop right there, because that is speculation. It's a theory. A guess. Something Kinew apparently believed might explain what was happening. Premiers are allowed to speculate, although one might reasonably expect the head of a provincial government to make it abundantly clear when he's doing so. Maybe he's right. Maybe he isn't. Unless somebody from MI6 rappelled through the Premier's window overnight and left a dossier marked FOR WAB'S EYES ONLY, the rest of us still require evidence.

But then, on March 24, something remarkable had happened. Kinew declared, “They started this war as a distraction from the Epstein files.”

Oh. They did?

Apparently the dossier arrived. Somewhere between maybe and definitely, our Premier appears to have been promoted to 00-Wab. Licence to Speculate.

So what happened in between? What new evidence emerged? What intelligence briefing established the motive? Which documents proved it? Who confirmed it? Because we're no longer talking about a premier tossing out a theory. We're talking about the Premier of Manitoba publicly accusing the President of the United States of starting a war to conceal or distract from the Epstein files.

That is an extraordinary accusation against any president. Making it against Donald Trump, of all presidents, adds another layer of bewilderment. Whatever anyone thinks of Trump, his tendency to respond aggressively to personal attacks is hardly classified information. The man has turned taking things personally into something resembling foreign policy.

Canadian governments are simultaneously trying to manage an already difficult relationship with the United States, our largest trading partner, while provincial premiers including David Eby, Kinew and Doug Ford seem remarkably comfortable supplying fresh reasons for that relationship to become even more antagonistic.

This isn't an argument that Canadian politicians should be frightened of Donald Trump or refrain from criticizing him. Criticize his tariffs. Criticize his foreign policy. Criticize his decisions until the microphones wear out. But accusing him of deliberately starting a war to distract from Jeffrey Epstein is something else entirely.

If Kinew has evidence establishing that, produce it. If he doesn't, what in God's name is the Premier of Manitoba doing stating it publicly as fact In the arena of public opinion?

Because somewhere along the way Kinew simply vaulted over the rather important evidentiary chasm between “I suspect” and “I know,” apparently without noticing there was supposed to be a bridge. I find that genuinely astonishing.

When the Premier of Manitoba makes an accusation this serious in front of reporters, Canadians should not have to wonder whether we're hearing information supported by evidence or Wab Kinew's personal hunch with the authority of the Premier's Office stapled to it.

Three days later came the federal NDP convention. Kinew told the crowd: “No American child from the blue collar or the middle class should have to die in Iran. Let the Epstein class fight the Epstein war.”

And they gave him a standing ovation.

The line landed to raucous applause, with people actually getting to their feet to cheer. Evidence, apparently, was no longer required. 00-Wab had briefed the room.

Christ, even M made Bond bring back the bloody photographs.

Because apparently Canada's political culture has deteriorated to the point where nobody in that cheering room thought to ask the terribly unfashionable question: Is any of this actually proven?

Instead, clap clap clap, honk honk, blah blah Epstein, and off we go.

Then Epstein somehow wandered into Manitoba's liquor policy. During an April interview about what it would take to put American alcohol back on Manitoba shelves, Kinew suggested upping the ante by demanding release of the Epstein files before removing the booze ban.

Excuse me, but how in the hell did we get here?

At this point I can only assume Q Branch had quietly taken over the Premier’s Office. Somewhere beneath the Legislature, a nervous civil servant was presumably handing 00-Wab an exploding briefcase marked EPSTEIN: TOP SECRET, while Q demonstrated a fountain pen capable of detecting inconvenient gaps in evidence and warned him, “Careful, Premier. That detects missing evidence. It doesn’t magically create it.”

I realize that sounds ridiculous. That's rather the point. Because spontaneously slipping up once or twice, fine. Politicians make provocative comments. They troll, and they exaggerate. They say something stupid because somebody put a television camera within fifty feet of them. But Kinew… Kinew keeps doing it.

It's always the same pattern with this man, and every time he returns to the subject, he sounds a little more certain than he did the last time. What began as maybe this explains it somehow became this is what happened, without that annoying little part in the middle where somebody is supposed to produce undeniable evidence.

A suspicion became a theory. The theory became a claim. The claim became a slogan. And eventually, the slogan became something he apparently felt perfectly comfortable repeating as factual, gospel truth.

And now, on September 9, we get this: “Release the Epstein files. Donald Trump is Jeffrey Epstein's best friend. The reason why we're at war in Iran and everyone's paying higher gas prices is because of the Epstein files.”

Sweet merciful Christ. 00-Wab has cracked the whole operation. Epstein. Trump. Iran. The war. Gas prices. It’s all right there.

Apparently somewhere between Winnipeg and Tehran, Manitoba’s Premier parachuted from a burning helicopter, skied down a mountain in a tuxedo, seduced a double agent, recovered the microfilm, escaped an exploding submarine and returned to the Legislature before Question Period carrying intelligence unavailable to the rest of Western civilization.

And apparently the only thing he forgot to bring back was the f*cking evidence.

Now back here on boring old Planet Earth, there are established facts. Trump knew Jeffrey Epstein socially. Their past association is documented. Epstein was a convicted sex offender whose crimes and relationships with powerful people unquestionably deserve investigation.

Fine. Investigate everything. Release everything legally releasable. Prosecute anybody against whom admissible evidence establishes a crime. That's how a functioning society is supposed to work.

But “Trump knew Epstein” and “Trump started a war to distract everyone from Epstein” are not the same statement.

There is an enormous evidentiary canyon between them. You don't get to bridge it with suspicion, repetition and a sufficiently confident tone of voice. And you certainly don't get to declare yourself safely on the other side simply because nobody stopped you.

And what should bother every Manitoban most: if this is how Kinew gets from “I think” to “I know” when he's talking about Donald Trump, what happens when the subject is something he actually has the power to decide? If Wab Kinew is this comfortable publicly converting inference into certainty, what standard does he apply when somebody walks into the Premier's Office with an allegation? What does he require before accepting advice? Before judging somebody's motives? Before making policy? Before spending public money? Before making decisions affecting businesses, families or communities?

Those aren't rhetorical cheap shots. They're questions about judgment.

A premier should have unusually good judgment. He should be difficult to fool. He should be skeptical. He should demand evidence. He should understand the difference between possible, plausible, probable and proven without needing somebody from the Justice Department to draw him a freaking diagram.

Maybe somewhere beneath the Manitoba Legislature there really is a subterranean command centre with a giant map of Iran, a shark tank and an unnecessarily complicated conference table that slowly rotates into the floor. If so, somebody please take me downstairs. I have questions for M. Otherwise we're left with the considerably less entertaining possibility that Kinew simply believes this.

And then there's the applause. I'm not sure which troubles me more: that Kinew keeps saying this stuff, or that thousands of Canadians hear it and respond like seals waiting for somebody to throw another Epstein-shaped herring onto the stage.

Wake up. We've got massive problems in this country.

You can despise Donald Trump and still demand evidence. You can believe every Epstein document should be released and still demand evidence. You can oppose the Iran war and still demand evidence. Those positions are not contradictory. They're what intellectual adulthood looks like.

And Manitoba voters should seriously consider what they're watching. Is this what you elected? Did you elect a premier to govern Manitoba, or did Manitoba accidentally elect 00-Wab, Her Majesty's Secret Premier, licensed to roam the international stage solving geopolitical mysteries before returning to Winnipeg in time for Cabinet?
Because at some point this stops being funny.

His office matters. His words travel outside Manitoba and outside Canada. Foreigners hearing a Canadian premier confidently announce unproven motives for an American war aren't necessarily thinking, What a courageous truth-teller. Some of them are probably wondering what the hell happened to us. And frankly, so am I.

Wab Kinew can hate Trump. He can demand the files. He can condemn the war. He can campaign against American tariffs. But he needs to stop using the authority of the Premier's Office to elevate whatever he personally believes into established fact.

Maybe I'm being unfair. Maybe somewhere behind Kinew's desk there's a bookcase that swings open at midnight, revealing a steel staircase descending beneath the Manitoba Legislature.

Maybe down there is a windowless situation room where M waits beside a glowing map while Q wheels out a tricked-out snowmobile with machine guns behind the headlights and a licence plate that rotates between FRIENDLY MANITOBA and FOR WAB'S EYES ONLY. Maybe a beautiful double agent arrives from Tehran carrying the missing documents in a briefcase handcuffed to her wrist.

Maybe Kinew receives his instructions, straightens his tuxedo, downs a martini, walks through the secret tunnel beneath Broadway and emerges beside the Golden Boy just as the Manitoba Legislature explodes behind him for absolutely no defensible reason.

If that's happening, I owe the man an apology. If it isn't, we're back to asking where the hell his evidence is.

Because leadership requires something considerably more difficult than certainty. It requires knowing when you don't know.

If Wab Kinew possesses evidence establishing that Donald Trump started a war to distract from the Epstein files, then by all means, produce the damn thing. Surely after all this international espionage, 00-Wab can emerge from the vault with something more substantial than his own certainty. Have Q retrieve the microfilm, get M on the secure line, drag the Aston Martin around front and tell Moneypenny lunch is cancelled. Hell, if somebody absolutely has to escape an exploding submarine or send a henchman skiing magnificently off a cliff before Manitobans are finally permitted to see the evidence, apparently that's where we are now.

Just produce the evidence, Premier. 

Because until you do, you're not James Bond. You're the Premier of Manitoba standing in front of television cameras telling Canadians that your personal theory about the President of the United States is established fact. And no amount of confidence changes that.

Wab Kinew may have given himself a Licence to Speculate, but Manitobans gave him a licence to govern. Perhaps it's time he remembered which one is real.

text:
In 2016 Bill Clinton said he had a deal Arafat turned down that would have given Palestinians all of Gaza and about 96–97% of the West Bank, plus land swaps. He blamed “they,” meaning the Palestinian leadership at Camp David, for rejecting it. He did not say they only wanted to kill Jews.

In October 2024 Clinton talked about that offer again (he said about 96% of the West Bank plus land in Israel). Then he said Hamas “did not care about a homeland for the Palestinians. They wanted to kill Israelis and make Israel uninhabitable.” Not “Palestinians.” Not “the Jews.”

So the meme stitches two real remarks into one fake quote.

However, it is not a lie that Clinton thinks Arafat walked away from a state, or that he thinks Hamas wants Israel gone.

text:
The Overmountain Men Invoke the Sword of the Lord and Gideon —

Major Patrick Ferguson’s threat against the western settlements helped inspire a military response among the frontier Patriots. Isaac Shelby, an experienced frontiersman and soldier, received Ferguson’s message from Samuel Phillips after Shelby and his men had returned across the mountains following the American defeat at Camden. 

Shelby rode about 40 miles to meet John Sevier, Commander of the Washington County militia. After discussing the danger facing their isolated settlements, Shelby and Sevier decided that an immediate offensive offered their best defense.

Shelby and Sevier needed additional troops before they could challenge Ferguson. They contacted Colonel William Campbell of Virginia and Colonel Charles McDowell of North Carolina. Campbell initially preferred to defend the frontier and allow Ferguson to move farther from General Charles Cornwallis. Shelby urged him to reconsider, arguing that the expedition needed Campbell’s men. Campbell agreed, as did McDowell, and the leaders called for a general gathering at Sycamore Shoals on the Watauga River on September 25.

The expedition also required money and supplies. John Adair allowed Sevier to use public funds belonging to North Carolina, while Sevier and Shelby personally promised repayment of the approximately $12,000 or $13,000 used for ammunition and supplies. Frontier communities ground corn into meal, produced gunpowder, mined lead, gathered livestock and horses, and prepared clothing for the soldiers.

More than 1,000 settlers gathered at Sycamore Shoals. Sevier brought 240 men, Shelby approximately 240, Campbell 400 and McDowell 160. Other militia forces planned to join them during the march. The army traveled without uniforms or an organized supply train, and many men carried long rifles, blankets and simple provisions.

On September 26, Clergyman Samuel Doak prayed for the expedition and gave the soldiers the battle cry, “The sword of the Lord and of Gideon!” The men then mounted their horses and rode across the mountains in search of Ferguson.

1. Gathering of the Overmountain Men at Sycamore Shoals by Lloyd Branson. Source: Tennessee State Museum Website.

text:
FLORIDA MAN OFFERS COPS A VODKA SPRITZER DURING 100 MPH CHASE

FORT MYERS, FLORIDA — Dennis Kravitz, 52, was arrested Friday night after allegedly leading deputies on a high-speed chase reaching over 100 miles per hour, then slowing just enough to hand a freshly mixed vodka spritzer out the window to the pursuing patrol car.

Deputies say the offer came as a genuine surprise mid-pursuit.

Deputies reported Kravitz had a small cooler and mixing setup visible on the passenger seat throughout the chase
Witnesses say he slowed to nearly a stop at one point specifically to extend the drink toward the patrol car window
He allegedly shouted "no hard feelings, it's a good batch" before speeding off again
Deputies say the spritzer itself was garnished with a lime wedge, prepared with clear care despite the circumstances
Witnesses reported he attempted the same offer a second time roughly two miles later, with a fresh drink
He reportedly told officers after his eventual arrest that he "just wanted the chase to feel civil"

The chase ended when Kravitz's vehicle ran low on fuel roughly fifteen miles from where it began.

"In nineteen years in law enforcement, I've been through plenty of pursuits, but never one that included a hospitality offer," said Deputy Sheriff Glen Ashworth, a 19-year veteran of the Lee County Sheriff's Office.

Both spritzers were logged into evidence, still cold. Neither was accepted.

He offered drinks mid-chase. Deputies offered handcuffs instead.
Some gestures simply don't land at a hundred miles an hour.

text:
In memory of Lorraine D. Antigua
September 27, 1968 – September 11, 2001

Age 32 Middletown, New Jersey, Cantor Fitzgerald, Securities Lending North Tower, 104th floor

Lorraine was a mother, a fiancée, a colleague people liked to sit near, and a woman who had already built a life she was proud of. She had two children, Aaron and Caitlin. She was engaged to Brian Wilkes. 

They had bought a house together in Middletown and were planning a family under one roof. They planted azaleas and sunflowers in the garden. They talked about getting married on a Harley, maybe at a drive-through chapel in Las Vegas. She said she would buy the bike.

She loved her work. Friends said she turned down other offers because she liked the securities lending desk at Cantor Fitzgerald. She had started young, working at the World Trade Center as a teenager in a co-op program at First Boston and she stayed in that world. 

People remembered her smile first. She came in bright. She was generous, an avid reader, a scuba diver. She made fried rice for the kids the night of September 10.

On the morning of September 11 she was at her desk on the 104th floor when American Airlines Flight 11 struck the North Tower. At 8:50 a.m. she left a message on Brian’s phone: a plane had hit her building, but she was okay. He never reached her again. No one from Cantor Fitzgerald who was in the firm’s offices that morning survived.

Those who knew her still speak of her in the present tense. “She’s awesome,” Brian said. “She ruined me for other women.” Friends recalled lunches, margaritas with no salt, a striped sweater and a fisherman’s hat at a barbecue two days before. Her mother remembered a daughter who had come out of Brooklyn and built something of her own.

Lorraine D. Antigua is remembered as a woman who loved her children, her work, her garden, and the life she was still making. 

Lorraine is not forgotten.
Never forget.❤️🙏

text:
Happy Birthday Betsy Drake
One of the most promising and unique actresses of her generation, Drake gave up stardom to marry Cary Grant. Wouldn’t we all? Betsy was the eldest child of American expatriates, and was born in Paris. Her grandfather, Tracy Drake, had opened the Drake Hotel in Chicago on New Year's Eve, 1920, but the family lost their money in the 1929 stock-market crash. As a result, Betsy returned to the U.S. with her parents, brothers, and a nanny. She grew up in Chicago, Connecticut, Washington, DC, Virginia and New York City, attending 12 different schools, before taking acting lessons at The National Park Seminary. She began looking for work in New York, supporting herself by modelling, and soon met the playwright Horton Foote, who offered her a job as an understudy in “Only the Heart”. After coming to the attention of producer Hal Wallis, Drake was pressured by her agent into signing a Hollywood contract. She loathed the film community and managed to engineer her release by pretending to be insane. Drake returned to New York, and, in 1947, read for Elia Kazan for the lead role in the play “Deep Are the Roots”. Later that year, Drake was selected by the director as one of the founding members of the Actors Studio. Cary Grant spotted her in 1947 while she was performing for Kazan in London. The couple, who both happened to be returning to the U.S. on the Queen Mary, were instantly attracted to one another. Drake was petite, beautiful, clever and had a huskily sexy voice. At Grant’s insistence, she was signed to a film contract by RKO  and David Selznick. In her first picture, she appeared opposite Grant, in the romantic comedy “Every Girl Should Be Married” (1948). A natural on screen, she won rave reviews for her droll performance. New York Times film critic Bosley Crowther called her “a lovely actress….foxily amusing….and more than a match for Mr Grant.” The world was now her oyster, but she rejected the film offers that came in for another offer entirely. On Christmas Day, 1949, Drake and Grant married in a private ceremony organized by the star’s best man, Howard Hughes. The couple chose a low-key if eccentric domestic life. They experimented with transcendentalism, mysticism, yoga and LSD. In 1954, they bought the "Las Palomas" estate in Palm Springs, California. House guests included good friends David Niven, who adored Betsy, and Randolph Scott. The Grants co-starred in the radio series “Mr. and Mrs. Blandings”, and appeared together in the comedy drama “Room for One More” (1952). Drake took leading roles in England and the U.S. and a supporting role in the film “Will Success Spoil Rock Hunter?” (1957). All was fair weather until Grant was hit by the Italian bombshell Sophia Loren, and fell hard whilst working with her in Spain. His next film was supposed to be “Houseboat” (1958). Betsy had written the script under a pseudonym for herself and her husband. Grant arranged for Loren to take Drake's place, with a rewritten screenplay. Their affair had already ended, however, which caused bitterness and tension on the set. Grant and Drake separated in 1958, and divorced in 1962. Their marriage was the actor’s longest and happiest union and he was a fool to have become involved with Loren. Grant credited Betsy with broadening his interests beyond acting, and with introducing him to LSD therapy and hypnosis. Drake herself took LSD as a way of recovering from the trauma of the divorce. She never remarried. Betsy Drake Grant spent the latter part of her life in London, where she died, aged 92, on October 27, 2015. Her last screen appearance was in the documentary film “Cary Grant: A Class Apart” (2005), in which she reflected on their  time together, and denied rumors that he was a homosexual.

text:
California Governor Gavin Newsom vetoed the bill that would have allowed undocumented immigrants to apply for state-backed home loans. [1] 
## What the Bill Proposed

* The Measure: Assembly Bill 1840 (AB 1840) aimed to clarify that applicants could not be disqualified from the [California Dream for All](https://t.co/tkWEWbDVXX) program solely based on their immigration status. [1, 2] 
* The Assistance: The program offers shared-appreciation loans for up to 20% of a home's value or a maximum of $150,000 for down payments and closing costs. [2, 3] 
* Repayment: Borrowers are required to pay back the original loan amount plus a share of the home's appreciation when selling or refinancing. [3, 4] 

## The Veto

* The Decision: Governor Newsom vetoed the legislation in September 2024.
* The Reason: Newsom cited finite state financial resources and budget constraints as the reason for rejecting the expansion of the program. [1, 5] 

[1] [https://t.co/C1aOtY5uWT](https://t.co/6MkUWDTKD0)
[2] [https://t.co/FlucFHIOZ1](https://t.co/0jGlKR2fMq)

  That is correct. Governor Gavin Newsom did not cite immigration status as his reason for vetoing the bill.
In his official veto message, he focused strictly on fiscal constraints. He stated:

"Given the finite funding available for CalHFA programs, expanding program eligibility must be specified within the annual budget process to ensure we mitigate impact to funding priorities. For this reason, I am returning this bill without my signature."

The veto was driven by the state's budget deficit and the fact that the California Dream for All program already faces severe funding shortages, often exhausting its entire multi-million dollar lottery budget within days.

The Deeper Political Crisis in America Reflected by California’s "Shelley Bill"
This article serves as an extension and deeper exploration of yesterday's discussion on the California State Legislature passing the so-called "Shelley Bill." In my book The Course of Western Civilization and numerous essays, I have repeatedly argued a core thesis: the American electoral system is not a rootless tree. It is deeply rooted in the fertile soil of Christianity, and it has existed, endured, and functioned soundly only because its electorate was grounded in devout, morally upright Christians. Once severed from this soil—as the electorate undergoes widespread de-Christianization and moral disintegration—America's democratic system inevitably loses its foundation, collapsing into an inefficient, corrupt, and even farcical political theater. In other words, detached from Christian civilization, American society loses all its virtue; only a revival of faith can rebuild America’s spiritual backbone and make America great again.
The fundamental reason the American electoral system has operated smoothly over the past two centuries lies in the intrinsic alignment between its core tenets and Christian doctrines:
Universal Equality: Rooted not in secular egalitarianism, but in the transcendental biblical truth that all human beings are created by God and stand equal before Him.
Procedural Integrity and Non-Fraudulence: The demand for credible, honest elections directly mirrors the commandment in the Decalogue: "Thou shalt not bear false witness."
The Inviolability of Private Property: Aligned with the biblical commandments "Thou shalt not steal" and "Thou shalt not covet," instilling reverence for individual fruits of labor and the sanctity of contracts.
Diligence and Self-Reliance: Deeply anchored in the biblical principle that "if anyone is not willing to work, let him not eat"—an ethic that condemns indolence and promotes honest labor.
Only when the majority of voters in a society, constrained by faith, cultivate universal civic virtues of self-discipline, integrity, and reverence can the American electoral system operate with genuine reliability and efficacy, yield benign outcomes, and advance societal flourishing.
Furthermore, Christianity offers a clear-eyed and profound diagnosis of human nature: total depravity and original sin. Severed from the constraints of faith, secular human nature—devoid of fear and trembling—is inherently selfish, greedy, decadent, opportunistic, and slothful. Because traditional American moral order was forged through Christianity, abandoning faith causes the virtues once sustained by it to be rapidly superseded by the indulgence of human weakness:
When the moral maxim of honoring labor—"he who does not work shall not eat"—is discarded, welfare-dependent underclass populism and a public-coffers-draining parasitic elite surge to dominance.
When the sacred commandment "thou shalt not bear false witness" is deconstructed, electoral fraud and the weaponization of justice are embraced as legitimate political maneuvers.
When the electorate regresses from "self-reliant, God-fearing guardians of the social contract" into an "indolent, rent-seeking collective dependent on fiscal transfers," this collapse leaves the voting base composed of a morally unmoored, corrupted populace.
Consequently, the American electoral system inevitably veers toward its opposite—becoming an instrument that legally disenfranchises the lawful and shields the lawless. If this occurs, does such a system even have a reason to exist?
Countless real-world political crises corroborate this civilizational trajectory, and California's aggressive push for the "Shelley Bill" offers a vivid footnote to my argument. When a massive coalition of rent-seeking classes and parasitic institutions secures absolute political hegemony, it does not merely mobilize ballots to install agents tailored to serve this corrupt nexus of interests. It goes further, abusing legislative power to silence whistleblowers, conceal corruption, and evict oversight. Consumed by a collective frenzy devoid of spiritual restraint, they conspire to purge any remaining "watchmen" who adhere to honest rules.
This reality once again eloquently demonstrates: institutions are merely instruments; faith is the soul. Stripped of its Christian foundation, the American system cannot secure liberty or safeguard justice. Instead, amid the bottomless descent of unchecked human nature, it will inevitably march toward self-dissolution and moral ruin.

text:
The Trump administration offered Cuba a major energy deal earlier this year: U.S. oil and investment in Cuba’s failing power infrastructure in exchange for privatizing state oil company CUPET and removing President Miguel Díaz-Canel, according to the Miami Herald.

The proposal came after Maduro’s capture ended free Venezuelan oil and Mexico stopped shipments, leaving Cuba increasingly fuel-starved.

U.S. emissaries secretly negotiated with Raúl Castro’s grandson, Raúl Guillermo Rodríguez Castro. Washington preferred full U.S. ownership of CUPET but considered joint ventures with Cuba or other investors; any deal also had to address ExxonMobil’s property claims against CUPET and CIMEX. 

Cuba, which produces only about 40% of its energy needs, would have gained reliable fuel and investment while Washington became its main oil supplier.

The talks collapsed because Havana feared dependence on a U.S.-controlled energy company, while Rodríguez Castro was open to economic reforms but rejected U.S. demands over Cuba’s leadership. 

“The Cubans were not there yet,” a source said. The negotiations also triggered backlash from Cuban-American Republicans concerned about preserving the Castro system, while Rodríguez Castro faced criticism in Cuba after his role and lavish lifestyle became public.

From Karl Streed -

I BET YOU DIDN'Y KNOW ABOUT THIS: AFTER FLIGHT 77 HIT THE PENTAGON ON 9/11, THE FOLLOWING HAPPENED.

A daycare facility inside the Pentagon had many children, including infants who were in heavy cribs. The daycare supervisor, looking at all the children they needed to evacuate, was in a panic over what they could do.

There were many children, mostly toddlers, as well as the infants who would need to be taken out with the cribs. There was no time to try to bundle them into carriers and strollers.

Just then a young Marine came running into the center and asked what they needed. After hearing what the center director was trying to do, he ran back out into the hallway and disappeared. The director thought, "Well, here we are, on our own."

About 2 minutes later, that Marine returned with 40 other Marines in tow.

Each of them grabbed a crib with a child, and the rest started gathering up toddlers.

The director and her staff then helped them take all the children out of the center and down toward the park near the Potomac .

Once they got about 3/4 of a mile outside the building, the Marines stopped in the park, and then did a fabulous thing - they formed a circle with the cribs, which were quite sturdy and heavy, like the covered wagons in the Old West.

Inside this circle of cribs, they put the toddlers, to keep them from wandering off. 

Outside this circle were the 40 Marines, forming a perimeter around the children and waiting for instructions. There they remained until the parents could be notified and come get their children.

The chaplain then said, "I don't think any of us saw nor heard of this on any of the news stories of the day. It was an incredible story of our men there.” There wasn't a dry eye in the room.

The thought of those Marines and what they did and how fast they reacted; could we expect any less from them? It was one of the most touching stories from the Pentagon.

It's the military, not the politicians that ensures our right to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. 

It's the military who salutes the flag, who serves beneath the flag, and whose coffin is draped by the flag.

If you care to offer the smallest token of recognition and appreciation for the military, please pass this on and pray for our men and women, who have served and are currently serving our country, and honor the memory of those who have given the ultimate sacrifice!

God Bless The USA!

Never forget!!!

text:
Your professor just told you the quiet part of the last sixty years.  Quanta Cura is, on his own admission, a solemn papal act, then he adds that nobody holds it anymore.  That is not continuity, but the definition of treating a defined condemnation as a reformable dead letter.  By this very theology : arianism, monophysitism,  monothelitism, protestantism, jansenism and all solemny condemned heretical doctrines could now become doctrine  -  which is exactly what the Vatican II latrocinium introduced by its imposition of the synthesis of all heresies.

To boldy say 'Nobody holds Quanta Cura anymore' is not historical sophistication, it is heretical depravity dressed as pastoral realism.  DH does not 'develop' Quanta Cura - it asserts the exact proposition Pius IX condemned, then builds a civil and ecclesial system on top of it.

On 8 December 1864 Pius IX, as pastor of the universal Church, by his apostolic authority reproved, prescribed, and condemned the claim that liberty of conscience and of worship is a proper right of every man, which must be proclaimed and asserted by law in every well-constituted society.  He made this doctrinal definition :

Itaque omnes et singulas (3) pravas opiniones ac doctrinas singillatim **hisce Litteris** commemoratas (2) auctoritate Nostra Apostolica (1) reprobamus, proscribimus atque damnamus, easque (4) ab omnibus Catholicæ Ecclesiæ filiis, veluti reprobatas, proscriptas atque damnatas omnino (1) haberi volumus et mandamus.

Quanta Cura is EX CATHEDRA because Pius IX (1) made definitive and binding condamnation (2) as Pastor and Teacher of all Christians and in virtue of his supreme Apostolic authority (3) regarding faith or morals (4) to be held by all the Church. He who refuses to accept the solemn definitions of the Pope, or who even doubts them, sins against faith; and should he remain obstinate in this unbelief, he would no longer be a Catholic, but a heretic:

We teach and define as a divinely revealed dogma that
when the Roman pontiff speaks EX CATHEDRA,that is, when,
in the exercise of his office as shepherd and teacher of all Christians,
in virtue of his supreme apostolic authority,
he defines a doctrine concerning faith or morals to be held by the whole church,
he possesses,by the divine assistance promised to him in blessed Peter,
that infallibility which the divine Redeemer willed his church to enjoy in defining doctrine concerning faith or morals.
Therefore, such definitions of the Roman pontiff are of themselves, and not by the consent of the church, irreformable.
So then, should anyone, which God forbid, have the temerity to reject this definition of ours: let him be anathema.
-PASTOR AETERNUS.

Quanta Cura and the Syllabus of Errors form a single integrated document. Quanta Cura contains the general doctrine, arranged in chapters while its Syllabus contains the specific condemned propositions, arranged in canons or in elenchus form - together they are one program. The encyclical establishes the doctrine itself while the Syllabus specify the particular errors that contradict said defined doctrine. This unity of structure means the four marks of an ex cathedra pronouncement apply across both parts as a coherent teaching act.

The First Vatican Council's dogmatic constitution Dei Filius forbids giving defined doctrine another sense than the Church has given it:

N° III.  If anyone says that
it is possible that at some time, 
given the advancement of knowledge, 
a sense may be assigned to the dogmas
propounded by the church which is different
from that which the church has understood
and understands: let him be anathema.
-DEI FILIUS, CHAPTER 4. ON FAITH AND REASON

Dignitatis Humanae begins with a courtesy. It said that Religious Freedom "leaves untouched traditional Catholic doctrine on the moral duty of men and societies toward the true religion and toward the one Church of Christ" (DH 1). Keep that sentence in MIND ... It is the courtesy that makes the rest drinkable. 

Pius VI in Auctorem Fidei already condemned innovators which hide tortuous maneuvers under ambiguity, then by slight additions distort the confession necessary for salvation, and that the perverse meaning under the veil of ambiguity must be named : In order not to shock the ears of Catholics, the innovators sought to hide the subtleties of their tortuous maneuvers by the use of seemingly innocuous words such as would allow them to insinuate error into souls in the most gentle manner. Once the truth had been compromised, they could, by means of slight changes or additions in phraseology, distort the confession of the faith that is necessary for our salvation. Whenever it becomes necessary to expose statements that disguise some suspected error or danger under the veil of ambiguity, one must denounce the perverse meaning under which the error opposed to Catholic truth is camouflaged. "Leaves untouched" is the veil. What follows is the meaning.

In the same breath the Council says the one true religion "subsists" in the Catholic and Apostolic Church (DH 1; LG 8), and yet its companion texts place "elements of sanctification and of truth" outside her (LG 8; UR 3; NA 2). That is already Syll. prop. 16, 17, and 18: salvation in the observance of any religion, good hope for those not in the true Church, Protestantism as another form of the same true religion. If those outside the Church are means of sanctification, the city must be told that it may not treat the outside as a public disorder. Then DH 1 adds that the Council draws from the treasury of Tradition "new things that are in harmony with the things that are old." Harmony, here, means this: keep the nouns of the old duty, empty them of every public effect. If societies still owe honor to the one Church, they cannot be bound to title the cult of error. If they are bound to title it, the duty is a husk (Syll. prop. 55, 77, 79). The deposit does not grow a contradictory right outside the unity of defined dogma as Dei Filius forbade another sense of defined doctrine under anathema. "New things in harmony with the old," when the new thing is the civil right of error, is not growth. It is the old condemned under a new name.

Quanta Cura did not strike a place in time - it struck a system, just like Popes condemned all other heresies before. It named as a deliramentum and libertas perditionis the claim that liberty of conscience and of worship is a proper right of every man, which law must proclaim in every well-constituted society. (Syll. prop. 15) DH 2 recites the contradictory as if it were a discovery of the Gospel: the person has a right to religious freedom, rooted in dignity known from the Word of God and from reason, and this right must be recognized as a civil right. Dignity in the 'Pastoral' constitution (GS 12-22) is defined as the inviolable status of the person by reason, free will, and liberty of conscience. Quanta Cura had already named that liberty, once made a civil title, a liberty of perdition. DH 1 baptizes the modern "awareness" of it and the demand to act by one's own options (Syll. prop. 3, 4, 15). Reason as measure of the religious choice is not an ornament. It is the first principle. If reason without the rule of revealed truth is arbiter of the cult a man will publicly keep, the State has no remaining title to prefer the altar of Christ to the altar of the idol. What DH teaches in not only a doctrine contrary to defined dogma (eg definition on Papal Infallibility) - it imposes the modernist heresy as a rule of faith (cf. S. Pius X, Pascendi).

Watch how the principle locks itself. DH 2 says no one is to be forced against conscience, nor prevented from acting according to it, privately or publicly, alone or associated, within "just limits," and that this exemption persists even in those who do not fulfill the duty of seeking and adhering to the truth, provided a "just public order" remains. That last clause is the bolt on the door as Pius IX condemned the doctrine that the best condition of society is one in which public power has no duty to restrain offenders against the Catholic religion except when public peace requires it. DH 2 and DH 7 write that condemned exception as the only limit left (Syll. prop. 19, 24, 40, 55, 77, 79). The man who refuses the truth keeps the title. Error ceases to be a wound in the city. Error, heresy, apostsy and idolatry - even demon worship - becomes a God given right.

The civil right is not only the erring man. It is the erring body. Pius IX condemned the claim that it is no longer expedient that the Catholic religion be the religion of the State to the exclusion of other worship (Syll. prop. 24, 77), and the claim that strangers should by law enjoy the public exercise of their own peculiar worship in christendom (Syll. prop. 78). It condemned the further claim that civil liberty of every worship, and the full power of publishing any opinions, does not corrupt minds or spread the pest of indifferentism (Syll. prop. 79). DH 4-6 take the condemned claim and make it the charter of the sect as such. Communities, without distinction of true and false, must govern themselves by their own norms, honor the "supreme divinity" in public, teach, form ministers, hold goods, and display "the special value of their doctrine for organizing society and inspiring the whole of human activity" (DH 4). That is Syllabus (prop. 15, 16, 21, 77, 78, 79, 80) in one grant. Proposition 21 had already struck the assertion that the Church cannot define dogmatically that the Catholic religion is the only true religion - DH 1 does not need to recite that assertion. What it does no say, it puts into action. The word "subsists" can remain in DH 1. The law of DH 4 has already made it idle. The Council teaches one true religion in DH 1 as a false demonstration of integrity, yet in imposed its contrary are a rule of faith.

Once the sect is a subject of rights, the Church cannot remain what Quanta Cura defended. Pius IX (Syll. prop. 19) struck the claim that the Church is not a true and perfect society, free, with perpetual rights from her Founder, and that civil power may define those rights and their limits. The same Roman Pontiff (Syll. prop. 20) condemned the claim that ecclesiastical authority may not act without the government's assent as well as the claim that the Church has no power of using force, nor any temporal power, direct or indirect (Syll. prop. 24). DH 3 answers all three at once: the civil power exceeds its limits if it directs or impedes religious acts. The unique liberty of the Church is folded into a generic liberty that belongs equally to the conventicle (Syll. prop. 19, 21, 24). DH 13 then completes the exchange. Where the modern regime of religious liberty exists, the Church is said to find her ideal conditions (Syll. prop. 19, 55, 80). The liberty of truth and the civil liberty of error are offered as one and the same.

The State is rewritten to match. Quanta Cura condemned ruling the people as if religion were not there. 
That is Syll. prop. 55: Church separated from State, State from Church, as a principle. 
Syll. prop. 39 and 56 struck the recasting of public law as a mere catalogue of rights detached from the true cult. DH 6 makes the State's "essential duty" the protection and promotion of the inviolable rights invented in DH 2-5, including the rights of false communities. 
The common good becomes the set of conditions in which those rights are enjoyed by secular standards (Syll. prop. 39, 56, 77). 
DH 5 carries the same title into the house and the school: the family orders its religion and chooses its schools by its own conviction (Syll. prop. 15, 47, 48). City, hearth, and classroom become instruments of the same grant. 
DH 7 pretends to limit it, but the limits are circular as they must not touch the content of falsehood and they may only keep a peace that already includes the equal right of error to organize (Syll. prop. 77, 79) : "Just public order" is not the peace of Christ, but the peace of the new first principle of liberty, equality and fraternity defending itself.

Here the system becomes satanic and apostate in the proper sense. DH 3 still names the eternal law as the supreme norm. Then it lodges the perception of that law in the already solemny condemned doctrine of liberty conscience in Quanta Cura. Then it concludes that a man must not be prevented from acting according to that conscience in public (Syll. prop. 15, 79). To refuse the free public exercise of religion, once secular "public order" is safe, is called an injury to the person and to the order God Himself established (Syll. prop. 24, 77). Pius IX had condemned a proposition as an error that must not be held. DH 3 makes the contradictory a command of God upon Caesar. It is not giving unto Cesar what is Cesar's, but robbing God from what is trully God's. On that showing, the public law of Christian ages, and Leo X in Exsurge Domine, prop. 33 (condemning the claim that "to burn heretics is against the will of the Spirit"), would be injuries to the divine order. Prop. 33 does not turn the scaffold into a sacrament - it refuses the Lutheran claim that the Church's public defense of the faith is against the Holy Ghost. 

DH 3 takes the condemned side: the magistrate "exceeds his limits" if he impedes religious acts. The prince is no longer the minister of God for the true cult. He is the warden of every cult and the Devil (Syll. prop. 19, 55, 56). Auctorem Fidei and Exsurge Domine are not distant ornaments here for they are are the earlier names of the same war: evangelical diction thrown over the disarming of the Church, solemny condemned by the extraordinary pontifical magisterium. DH 3 teaches that disarming is obedience to God - thus every military action the Church perpetrated, the Holy Roman Inquisition and all the Roman Pontiffs who protected christendom are declare by DH to have sinned and err'd in their faith and morals. The system therefore writes itself a past. DH 9-12 say the doctrine is founded in Revelation, that Christ and the Apostles handed it on, that the Church has kept and transmitted it, and that former practices contrary to it failed the Gospel (Syll. prop. 5, 80). If fifteen centuries of public law were a failure to understand the Apostles, then it is implicit that the Church has imposed error since its very first ecumenical Council according to this heretical document.

This is why Pius IX had already condemned the claim that the Roman Pontiff can and ought to reconcile himself with progress, liberalism, and modern civilization. (Syll. prop. 80) DH 15 salutes international charters and modern constitutions as favorable signs and calls a juridical guarantee of religious liberty necessary for the peace of peoples (Syll. prop. 77, 79, 80). The world that hissed at the Syllabus is invited to countersign the Council. Dignity founds the right. The right founds the new common good. The new common good founds the new history. The new history founds the claim that this was always the Gospel. The serpent has its tail in its mouth.

Then the last exchange. DH 14-15 still calls for the (Montinian) Church to teach (its heresies) to all nations, inside a legal order that has already armed every false religion with the same civil title to teach, recruit, and form society (Syll. prop. 15, 16, 21, 79). The command remains. The forum is given to the contradiction of the command. The text ends by asking that, under a regime of religious liberty, the human family reach the freedom of the children of God. The liberty Pius IX named a liberty of perdition is offered as the road to glory (Syll. prop. 15, 16, 80). The condemned means is baptized as the instrument of the supernatural end.

We must see this doctrine as one beast, not as a simple list of errors. Dignity as civil title, even in the man who refuses the truth (Syll. prop. 3, 15), begets a new subject of rights: the erring conscience and the false community as such (Syll. prop. 15, 16, 21, 77). That subject forces a new Caesar: protector of those rights, forbidden to impede the cults that deny Christ (Syll. prop. 19, 24, 39, 55, 56, 77). The new Caesar requires a new memory: the old condemnations were immaturity (Syll. prop. 5, 80). The new memory requires a new mission: preach Christ in a square that must legally protect the contradiction of Christ (Syll. prop. 16, 21, 79). DH 2 is the heart. Open it and every later number is only pulse. Close it and nothing remains but the courtesy of DH 1.

The first is heresy against a solemn condemnation. The second is heresy plus the reduction of the Church from perfect society to licensed tenant. The third is the method that keeps the words "Revelation," "Apostles," "Tradition," and drains them, and calls the draining "development." Auctorem Fidei told us to name the perverse meaning under the veil. The perverse meaning is this beast. Exsurge Domine, prop. 33, told us that to call the Church's public defense of the faith contrary to the Spirit is itself the condemned claim. DH 3 calls that defense an injury to the order of God. 

In most simple terms : if one accepts DH as doctrine → QC is denied or doubted = one would no longer be a Catholic, but a heretic. 

NO SUCH THING CAN COME FROM THE DIVENELLY ASSISTED VICAR OF CHRIST AND THE IMMACULATE BRIDE OF THE LAMB OF GOD.

What is your professor doing? He is doing what Saint Pius X called modernism when it meets a defined text it will not obey. Pascendi described the move: dogma is a vital expression that evolves with consciousness; yesterday's condemnation was true "for its time"; today's consciousness has further requirements. So Quanta Cura remains "formally binding" as a museum label, and "nobody holds it" as a living rule. That is the heretical hermeneutic of continuity - as it teaches that the Church can solemnly bind the faithful to a proposition and then educate them to ignore it. 

If the Church is infallible in her solemn definitions, those who reject the definitions lose the faith.

If the definitions may be shelved because the faculty no longer holds them, infallibility is a courtesy title. You asked how to see continuity? There is none to see.

Your professor's very comission of this act which signifies HERESY, e.g. statement of some doctrine contrary or contradictory to a revealed and defined dogma, gives sufficient grounds for the presumption for the crime of heresy.

May the Blessed Mother keep you.

text:
From Karl Streed -

I BET YOU DIDN'Y KNOW ABOUT THIS: AFTER FLIGHT 77 HIT THE PENTAGON ON 9/11, THE FOLLOWING HAPPENED.

A daycare facility inside the Pentagon had many children, including infants who were in heavy cribs. The daycare supervisor, looking at all the children they needed to evacuate, was in a panic over what they could do.

There were many children, mostly toddlers, as well as the infants who would need to be taken out with the cribs. There was no time to try to bundle them into carriers and strollers.

Just then a young Marine came running into the center and asked what they needed. After hearing what the center director was trying to do, he ran back out into the hallway and disappeared. The director thought, "Well, here we are, on our own."

About 2 minutes later, that Marine returned with 40 other Marines in tow.

Each of them grabbed a crib with a child, and the rest started gathering up toddlers.

The director and her staff then helped them take all the children out of the center and down toward the park near the Potomac .

Once they got about 3/4 of a mile outside the building, the Marines stopped in the park, and then did a fabulous thing - they formed a circle with the cribs, which were quite sturdy and heavy, like the covered wagons in the Old West.

Inside this circle of cribs, they put the toddlers, to keep them from wandering off. 

Outside this circle were the 40 Marines, forming a perimeter around the children and waiting for instructions. There they remained until the parents could be notified and come get their children.

The chaplain then said, "I don't think any of us saw nor heard of this on any of the news stories of the day. It was an incredible story of our men there.” There wasn't a dry eye in the room.

The thought of those Marines and what they did and how fast they reacted; could we expect any less from them? It was one of the most touching stories from the Pentagon.

It's the military, not the politicians that ensures our right to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. 

It's the military who salutes the flag, who serves beneath the flag, and whose coffin is draped by the flag.

If you care to offer the smallest token of recognition and appreciation for the military, please pass this on and pray for our men and women, who have served and are currently serving our country, and honor the memory of those who have given the ultimate sacrifice!

God Bless The USA!

Never forget!!!

text:
🚨 State of Laser Adress 🚨

It has been a rough week boys and girls, not gonna lie.

The deal for the workshop fell through. I am feeling all sorts of ways about it, but at this point there is really nothing I can do about it. The seller originally had the building listed for $140,000. Not a single person interested in it, and by the time we looked at it, the asking price was $110,000. After looking at the building, and see that it was very neglected over the last 50 years, we made an offer for $80,000. They countered with $100,000 and we agreed, because it would be affordable for us, and we had a vision of how we could take care of the neglect and make it our own. 

The bank approved everything, and as many of you know, if you are getting a loan for property, you need an appraisal. The bank and the appraiser took their time (it is S Louisiana and things move slow) but the appraisal finally came back, and it came in at $56,000. Much lower than I or the seller was expecting, but the appraisal was thorough and very detailed, and I agreed with it. With all the work that needed to get done, the appraisal was right. 

So, we sent our counter offer to the seller, and they did not agree. They wanted $80,000, and the bank will not loan anything over the appraised price. There would have been an option for us to pay the difference in cash, but that would have completely emptied our accounts from the money we were going to use to fix the place up. The seller was not willing to budge on the price (I know what I got sonny!) even though a professional appraiser was telling them otherwise. So, unfortunately we had to walk away. The whole ending put a very sour taste in my mouth about the building and seller, so I truly feel like I am dodging a bullet, but that is neither here nor there. 

This area doesn't have many options available when it comes to these types of workshops, so we are back on the search again. I am absolutely determined to be in a new workshop by the end of the year, even if it means buying a whole ass house and turning it into the House of Laser! 

NGL, the whole thing made me feel a bit depressed. I put every ounce of energy into making this place a reality, and it drained me. I pushed myself harder and further than I ever have, and the deal not working out sent my head spinning. 

So, in the meantime, we will be doing our normal thing, still putting out crispy lasered patches, mags and mugs, but the only downfall is that the FFL will have to wait. It WILL happen, just not at this very moment. 

It has been a long exhausting ride, and it will be again, but I want to say thank you to our whole community that we have built here. Literally none of this would have been possible without y'all. I appreciate each and every one of y'all more than you know. 

Laserman

text:
TL;DR -- your anxieties are understandable, and AI does bring some very real risks. That said, there are three very compelling reasons to believe that any extreme existential threat presented by AI is no different from the normal existential threats that humans ignore as incredibly unlikely.  Well, there's no conspiracy or narrative likely going on. Many of the tech individuals who are telling these stories are likely falling victim to echo chambers.

_____ 

Start by realizing that this entire narrative is designed specifically to manipulate you into having the feelings that you're having right now. People have predicted doomsday from a variety of new technological, biological, religious, and atmospheric phenomena throughout human history. 

To be clear, it's not stupidity. The people who develop these models are incredibly smart. They're very conscientious, and they genuinely do believe what they're saying. 

Instead, what we're seeing here is an emergent cultural phenomenon that is unique to Bay Area tech/Silicon Valley culture. There are several reasons to have a fair degree of confidence that this is more an emergent cultural phenomenon than a genuine belief based on statistics and outcomes that are actually likely to happen:

1. Consistent slogans and language: the format of posts regarding the danger of AI, recursive self-improvement, and artificial superintelligence is very consistent. It features a widely ranging percentage to represent the likelihood of human extinction and uses a variety of emotionally charged adjectives that tell you nothing about how the result came about and only tell you about how bad the end result is. Most of the posts pretty much leave it there and, for credibility, rely on their expert credentials, declining to offer a single concretized detail as to how this extinction-level event might or might not come about. Those posts that do offer some sort of vignette skip right to the moment before Armageddon is unleashed, painting some presumed Mary Sue picture of an AI that has somehow already gained access to some bio weapon, some lab, or some collection of chemicals. Not a single post I've seen ever makes any reference to the story, the mechanisms, or how we get from where we are today to systems of such weakness, vulnerability, and apparent lack of foresight. The engineers designing this critical infrastructure apparently just waved their hands in the air and said, "It'll be fine." 

2. That leads right into point number two: the consistent failure to describe any intermediate steps that condition the critical infrastructure that AI is supposedly so likely to be able to invade strongly suggests that those who espouse the opinion adopted it from others rather than arriving at it through a reasoned approach to first principles. A structured exercise of thinking about AI risk based on first principles without a preexisting narrative would necessarily encompass the comparatively basic task of considering what actions and interventions can and should be implemented right now to try to head off some of these risks. After all, there's no difference between identifying the vulnerability and identifying the item to be redressed. All of this suggests that these folks, incredibly high IQ and hardworking as they may be, are falling victim to echo chambers and groupthink. Moreover, many of them have an incredible virtue-signaling incentive to present themselves as effective altruists: the people who are "so earnestly trying to do the right thing when they could be off making money and being evil." But instead, they're really working hard, even though there are so many ethical dilemmas! And so, even though they're making millions and millions of dollars every single year, really, they're working for the good of humanity. 

3. Another important thing to consider (that isn't a primary motivator but must be articulated): OpenAI, and Anthropic have a lot to gain from increased regulation in the AI space. Right now, their gross profit margins on the AI services they sell to enterprises and individuals are fairly healthy, but competitors from China and elsewhere are catching up fast. We're starting to get to the point where there are fewer and fewer distinctions between the capabilities of the top models. If the product you're selling isn't distinguishable from the next guy's, then you're in a situation where your product has become a commodity. Whenever things get commoditized, the price decreases dramatically. OpenAI and Anthropic cannot survive as businesses if their profit margins on model services are in the low single digits, as is the case with most commodity markets. Something that can turn this fortune around is shrinking the number of players in the market by designating OpenAI and Anthropic as trusted partners and not allowing anybody else to play in the space of frontier model development. That is "regulatory capture."

text:
Two dates settle the argument about the traditional 60/40.

​In 2008, the S&P 500 took a 57% drawdown while core bonds held flat. In 2022, both plunged together, with core bonds down roughly 17%. Same two assets, completely different inflation regimes.

​The math is laid out in J.P. Morgan's Guide to the Markets:

• 1964 to 1999: correlation +0.28 (average inflation 4.86%)
• 2000 to 2020: correlation -0.31 (average inflation 2.13%)
• 2021 to 2025: correlation +0.33 (average inflation 4.52%)
• Full 60-year period: +0.08

​Stock-bond correlation tracks inflation. The negative correlation that made a two-asset portfolio feel like a free lunch was a 20-year anomaly inside a 60-year history. It only worked because inflation stayed anchored near 2%.

​David Kelly of J.P. Morgan drew the practical line: do not expect Treasuries to automatically bail out an equity drawdown in this regime.

​A portfolio concentrated in 60% U.S. large caps and 40% bonds leaves an allocator exposed to simultaneous drawdowns. The institutional playbook builds around true multi-asset diversification:

• Private Credit and Real Estate for contractual yield without duration volatility.
• Infrastructure for direct inflation pass-through.
• Multi-Strategy Hedge Funds for non-correlated alpha.
• Private Equity and global equity breadth (small cap, emerging) to eliminate concentration risk.

​Diversification is not owning 50 stocks in one index. It is owning cash flows that answer to fundamentally different economic regimes.

​Sources: J.P. Morgan Asset Management (Guide to the Markets, slide 64, data as of June 30, 2026), David Kelly ("The New, New Normal," September 8, 2026).

text:
IVAN,

DISINFORMATION IS NECESSARY 

GRACE GIVEN

RETURN OF INHERITANCE 

There was a country that used to treat its people like owners.

That was not a slogan. It was how the place was built. Families claimed land and expected their children to keep it. Hamilton wanted shops and mills here so the yield would stay here. Lincoln’s Homestead Act put title in ordinary hands. McKinley and the old tariff men said if a foreign workshop could undercut an American one, the American house would slowly empty. For a long time the deal was simple. You work. You build. The profit does not all leave by the docks.

Then the deal flipped.

Factories went overseas because labor was cheaper and the finance houses liked the margin. Towns that made steel, cloth, tools, and cars became warehouses for other people’s goods. Washington still collected taxes. Banks still collected interest. Shoppers got lower prices and called that winning, while the job that used to pay for the house left with the product. The citizen became a customer. The country became a platform. That is real history, not a parable. You can walk the boarded main streets and count it.

Older still is the biblical picture people reach for when they see that hollowing. In Israel the land was not supposed to be sold off the family forever. Every so often debts were released and fields came home. They called it jubilee. It was not a stimulus check. It was a law against becoming a tenant on your own ground. America never ran that calendar. It ran a rougher version: property, wages, and a border around the market.

That is what “return of inheritance” means in plain speech. Not a miracle envelope. The fruit of the country coming back to the people who live in it after a long season of managers, offshoring, and a government that treated households like a cost.

Tonight in Dallas, Trump put a number on that hunger. If Republicans keep the House and the Senate, he said, every adult citizen gets a $5,000 dividend, and it has to be spent in the United States. Hear it clearly. It is a campaign condition, not a check already in the mail. He has talked tariff dividends before. Those checks have not shown up. Five thousand dollars times every adult is a huge bill. It has to come from tariffs, growth, cuts, or new borrowing. If it is borrowed, it is not inheritance. It is a loan with a flag on it.

Still, the shape of the offer is the old American sentence: you are a shareholder in this house again. Spend the yield at home. Do not send it back down the road that emptied the towns.

That is the story without the fog.
Owners, then tenants, then a promise to put some of the fruit back on the table.
History will decide if the promise becomes a payment.
The hunger is already historical.

The Fiscal Eigenvalue: When Sovereign Debt Stops Converging
Public Doctrine Series · The Engineered Long End · Advanced Technical Companion III-A

There is one question that decides everything about a national debt, and it is almost never asked.

After a shock, does the system return toward a sustainable state — or does its own internal structure cause the pressure to persist and expand?

That is not a question about magnitudes. It is a question about convergence, and it has an exact answer.

Our preceding paper, The Arithmetic of Escape, established that a Treasury buyback may improve market functioning without repairing the fiscal mechanism that continually recreates pressure at the long end. This paper takes the argument deeper, and moves the doctrine from magnitude comparison to system design.

It introduces the exact sovereign debt-ratio law, and from it the Fiscal Eigenvalue — the multiplier that determines whether debt pressure decays or compounds. It defines the Convergence Residual, the measurable distance between a government's actual fiscal reaction and the reaction convergence would require. It formalises the refinancing-memory coefficient, which explains why today's interest burden is a weighted memory of past issuance decisions, and why deferral is expensive in a way no single-period comparison reveals. These compose into the GFE Fiscal State Vector [λ, Γ, q] — three numbers that state a sovereign's condition without recourse to adjectives.

The paper then applies the framework to the four ledgers of a Treasury buyback, and to the Washington–Tokyo control problem: two sovereigns, one coupled system, each optimising locally. It closes with the Sovereign Convergence Rule.

Its central conclusion is deliberately precise:

A market operation can alter liquidity.
A maturity operation can redistribute exposure through time.
A central-bank facility can contain funding stress.
But only an adequate fiscal reaction rule can change the long-run convergence condition.

Four instruments, four different variables. Only one reaches the fourth.

The OCD torment of having to juggle exploration versus being able to freely iterate and explore and connect and build the future is really triggering. Then you go on X and its a bunch of people somehow spending 4,000 dollars to play minecraft with some new model and you just sit back and have to think, what are we doing, what is the point of this all, and should we be earning power more than we pay for it. I mean why should some scam artist con man on X be allowed to buy 4000 dollars of the compute pool just to hit some target on social media, when some genius somewhere could be iterating to save humanity. You want to upsell something, upsell your business facing shit. I don't know why you allocate anything at all to Image and Video. Trust you me you are not going to fly to Mars on a stack of memes, only intelligence will get you there, something you could be harvesting more efficiently from people with a give and take system, where right now if I opt into data sharing like I have, its just you stealing my soul with zero reward to me. This whole system and every company iterating their abomination version of it is a carbuncle of absolute torment with flashing lights to keep the penguins happy along the way. 

Imagine this, I wake up one day, and I get an email, hey, with all the data you shared, you improved our model or technologies in X, Y, Z ways, we would like to immediately offer you a larger credit pool, and a coding grant to make and create products to help the world, where the product ideas you can even generate, like assigning a worker.  Now you are harvesting the real core of a human being, because you have their heart, so you will have their mind. A symbiotic relationship. Whatever this all is now, is a futile cancer. Especially @GeminiApp , idk what happened to them but its like a decaying fruit on the table that somehow regresses more with each day.  A sad dying dog, at least Xai is better than that, far better now.

ART
Art

At  the National Art Gallery in Dublin, a husband & wife were staring  at a portrait that had them completely confused.  The painting depicted  three black men totally naked sitting on a park bench. Two of the figures had black willies, but the one in the middle had a pink willie. 
 
The gallery curator realized that they were having trouble interpreting the painting & offered his assessment. He  went on for over half an hour explaining how it depicted the sexual  emasculation of black men in a predominately white, patriarchal society. In  fact, he pointed out, some serious critics believe that the pink Willie  also reflects cultural and sociological oppression experienced by gay  men in contemporary society.

After the curator left, an Irishman, approached the couple & said, would you like to know what the painting is really about?

Now why would you claim to be more of an expert than the curator of the Gallery asked the couple?

Because I'm the guy who painted it, he replied.

There are no black men depicted at all. They're three Irish coal miners. The middle guy went home for lunch.

The Israelis are known for loving life. We, on the other hand, sacrifice ourselves. We consider our dead to be martyrs.

The Israelis do not know that the Palestinian people has progressed in its research on death. Fathi Hammad (Hamas official, Al-Aqsa TV, 2008)

I hope to offer my only son as a martyr, just as his father was.

We realized that sport was the modern religion of the Western world. We knew that English and American audiences sitting in front of their television sets would not watch a programme showing the fate of the Palestinians if there was a sporting event on another channel. We offered human sacrifices to your gods of sport and television and they answered our prayers.

Palestinian terrorist (Munich Olympics, 1972)

This will be a war of extermination, a momentous massacre which will be spoken of like the Mongol invasions and the Crusades.

Azzam Pasha (Secretary-General of the Arab League; 1947)

Kill the Jews wherever you find them. This pleases God, history and religion. This saves your honour. God is with you. Haj Amin al-Husseini (Mufti of Jerusalem, Radio Berlin broadcast, 1944)

God grants a proud life in this world and eternal grace in the hereafter to a nation that perfects the industry of death and knows how to die nobly.

Hassan al-Banna (“The Industry of Death,” al-Nadhir, 1938)

Slaughter the Jews ! We await the order from Mufti al-Husseini!

The order has come from Haj Amin al-Husseini saying that now is the time to murder all Jews — from the youngest to the oldest. You may take the Jews’ women and possessions, in the name of Allah!

Hebron Arab leaders (proclamation, Hebron, 1929)

You Muslims! Here you have rich American Jews… Slaughter all Jews! Today is Islam’s day! This is the day the Prophet commanded us to observe! Allah and his messenger call upon you to avenge… Butcher the Jews… here are beautiful Jewish women.

Palestine is our land, the Jews are our dogs! We will drink the blood of the Jews.

 The Government is with us, Allenby is with us, kill the Jews; there is no punishment for killing Jews.

This was and will remain an Arab land… the Zionists will be massacred to the last man. Nothing but the sword will decide the future of this country.

Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties [in exchange] for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of Allah, so they kill and are killed. [It is] a true promise [binding] upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur’an…”

So let those fight in the cause of Allah who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter. And he who fights in the cause of Allah and is killed or achieves victory – We will bestow upon him a great reward.

And you had already known about those who transgressed among you concerning the Sabbath, and We said to them, ‘Be apes, despised. Those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry and made of them apes and pigs and slaves of Taghut.

Quran 2:65 / 5:60 / 7:166

Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful and who do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture – [fight] until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled.”

Koran 9:29

Abu Huraira reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:“The Last Hour would not come until the Muslims fight the Jews and the Muslims kill them, so that the Jews will hide behind a stone or a tree. The stone or the tree will say: ‘O Muslim, O servant of Allah, there is a Jew behind me; come and kill him.’ Except the Gharqad tree, for it is the tree of the Jews.”

Sahih Muslim 2922 (also Sahih al-Bukhari 2926 / 3593, 846- 875 AD)

The liberation of Palestine aims to “purify” the country of all Zionist presence.

PLO Charter (Article 15, 1964)

We must fight Evil at its source, and the main root of Evil is America. (…) Imam Khomeini, our leader, has repeatedly assured us that America is the source of all our ills and that it is the mother of intrigues. (…) The children of the Hezbollah nation in Lebanon are confronting [their enemies] in order to achieve the following objectives: a definitive Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon as a first step towards the total destruction of Israel and the liberation of Holy Jerusalem from the stain of occupation…

Hezbollah Charter (1985)

Israel exists and will continue to exist until Islam abolishes it as it abolished what preceded it.

Hassan al-Banna (preamble of the Hamas Charter, 1988)

The Islamic Resistance Movement is a distinct Palestinian movement that pledges allegiance to Allah and His path, Islam. It strives to raise the banner of Islam over every inch of Palestine.

Hamas Charter (Article 6, 1988)

A revolutionary regime must get rid of a certain number of individuals who threaten it, and I see no other means than death. One can always get out of a house. The revolutionaries of 1793 probably did not kill enough.

Jean-Paul Sartre, interview with Michel-Antoine Burnier in Actuel, 28 February 1973.This irrepressible violence, he shows perfectly, is not an absurd storm nor the resurrection of savage instincts nor even an effect of resentment: it is man himself recomposing himself. This truth we have known, I believe, and we have forgotten it: the marks of violence, no gentleness will erase them: it is violence alone that can destroy them. And the colonized heals himself of the colonial neurosis by driving out the colonizer with arms. When his rage explodes, he recovers his lost transparency, he knows himself to the exact extent that he makes himself; from afar we regard his war as the triumph of barbarism; but it proceeds by itself to the progressive emancipation of the fighter, it liquidates in him and outside him, progressively, the colonial darkness. As soon as it begins, it is without mercy. One must remain terrified or become terrible; that means: abandon oneself to the dissociations of a falsified life or conquer native unity. When the peasants touch guns, the old myths fade, the taboos are overthrown one by one: the fighter’s weapon is his humanity. For, in this first time of the revolt, one must kill: to shoot down a European is to kill two birds with one stone, to suppress at the same time an oppressor and an oppressed: there remain a dead man and a free man; the survivor, for the first time, feels a national soil under the soles of his feet.

Jean-Paul Sartre (preface to Frantz Fanon'sThe Wretched of the Earth, 1961)

We had all dreamed of it… Hamas did it.

Denis Leroy (known as Guezmer; cartoon caption in the Basque weekly Ekaitza, 13 September 2001 — referring to the 9/11 attacks)

That we dreamed of this event, that everyone without exception dreamed of it, because no one can fail to dream of the destruction of any power that has become so hegemonic — this is unacceptable to the Western moral conscience, but it is nevertheless a fact, and it is precisely measured by the pathetic violence of all the discourses that seek to erase it. At the limit, they did it, but it is we who wanted it.

Jean Baudrillard (September 2001)

That brains could achieve something in a single act that we in music could not even dream of, that people rehearsed like madmen for ten years, totally fanatically for a single concert, and then died. It is the greatest work of art possible in the entire cosmos. Imagine what happened there. There are people who are so concentrated on one performance, and then 5,000 people are driven into the beyond in a single moment. I could not do that. Next to that we are nothing, we composers… Imagine this, that I could create a work of art now and that you would all not only be astonished but that you would drop dead immediately, you would be dead and you would be born again, because it is simply too insane. Some artists also try to cross the limits of the possible or the imaginable, to wake us up, to open another world for us.

Karlheinz Stockhausen (September 2001)

The situation is tragic but the balance of forces in the Middle East means that in the long term Israel, like the Frankish kingdoms of old, will end up disappearing. This region has always rejected foreign bodies.

Dominique de Villepin (former French government official, minister and prime minister, 2001)

We will only have peace with the Arabs when they love their children more than they hate us.
