Preface
More Dutch than Welsh! Just a man on X (BRAT*/Veteran). British, English, Scottish 13%, Irish 12% (NI 3%), Isle of Man 3%, Dutch 3%, Nordic 2% and Welsh 2%. Members of my maternal family traced our ancestry back several hundred years. 

Given a Nordic element on my paternal side, it's not inconceivable that I'm a badass Viking and my forebears came to England in the late 700s or in 1066. 

†BRAT=British Regiment Attached Traveller (1956–74 (Veteran: Military 1973–86)). MOD (1991–93). Scroll down for Account Features, following on from Profile (History) ...

Profile (History) 
Ex-forces, former British soldier (Royal Electrical & Mechanical Engineers (REME)). During my time in the services, I deployed with multiple regiments, corps and REME Workshops (Wksp), including (but not exclusively) ...

... 3rd Light Infantry, Light Aid Detachment (LAD), Minden, West Germany, British Army Of The Rhine (BAOR*); REME Wksp, Fort George, Londonderry, Northern Ireland (NI (Tour of duty)); The Army Dog Unit (ADU NI), Royal Army Veterinary Corps (RAVC (HMP Maze, Long Kesh (Covert deployment), an elite task force pulled from various units or regiments of the army—in uniform we wore the famous 'Red Paw' in our berets)); The Household Cavalry, Windsor* (Blues & Royals (Royal Horse Guards and 1st Dragoons (RHG/D))), LAD; 28 Amphibious Engineer Regiment Wksp REME, Hameln (BAOR (Trade + Unit Technical Photographer—frustrated photo journalist)), and the School of Electrical & Mechanical Engineers (SEME (Small Arms)), Bordon, Hampshire, UK.

†NATO. †April '80–December '82: Ambulance cover, June '81; Hyde Park & Regent's Park bombings, 20 July '82.

I'm the youngest son of a then-serving soldier (BRAT) who was in demand for his engine removal and installation skills. My late father had been a REME Powerpack (Powertrain) Specialist, serving for many years with various Tank Regiments (latterly small arms)...

...Early doors, REME mechanics were graded A, B and C according to their trained, untrained skill level (A being the highest), which (1960s)* wharfed into A: Armour (requiring the highest skill level); B: Soft-skinned (Wheeled, generally); and C: Plant. Dad may have been unskilled initially, though I understood he trained as a C (Plant) Mechanic (Mech.), but was employed—for most of his army career—as an Armoured (A) Mech and, ultimately, as a Soft-skinned (B) Mech in his final years in London before completing his service. In his latter days, Dad was Chief Engineer for a heating company servicing nurseries in the East of England for many years (d. 2014).

†REME, formed 1 October 1942.

Some time before my 13th birthday, I was selected to play football for my school team, Castle Down, Tidworth. It was still 1968 (I think, but only just); I played my debut for the school (I recall we won convincingly), only to find my parents waiting with the car as the coach dropped me in the village. "Where have you been?" I recall them asking (Somewhat angrily), like it was yesterday. Then, off we went to a new home, and I never saw my school friends again (Aside from Barry Penn, whom I met up with again in the mid '70s when I was posted to a REME Wksp nearby).

In little over a year, we'd lived in a village in the South of England, moved lock, stock and barrel to Warminster and posted back to Germany before I was thirteen. Soon after, I started at a new BAOR School (Gloucester) in Hohne, watched the moon landing on the telly in Fallingböstel, West Germany, and competed at football in a German youth league before starting at yet another school in the East End of London, before my 14th b'day.

I've lived in various countries, including: Africa ('62–'65), Cyprus ('76), NI ('78–'80), Denmark ('81), the UK and many years on the European mainland (BAOR); in Berlin ahead of my first birthday, posted to Bergen-Hohne (minutes from Belsen (My first school)) before the Berlin Wall went up. I attended eleven schools in ten years, in Africa, BAOR and in the UK; had five* jobs before I joined the army in 1973 and was living in a Prisoner-of-war camp in Scotland—over from NI, exercising war dogs with the ADU—when Lord Louis Mountbatten was assassinated in 1979.

Quote: “From the ages of eight to 18, me and my family (my family and I moved around a lot. Mostly, we would just stretch, but occasionally one of us would actually get up to go to the fridge.” — Jarod Kintz, Author.

†My five jobs immediately after school, before I enlisted, included three major hotels in the West End, where I met several celebrities of the day, including but not exclusively, Bruce Forsyth, Ken Dodd, Lester Piggott, Mike Yarwood, Paul Cook*, Roger Whittaker and, the following year, Lionel Blair and a lift full of Southampton Football players staying at the Hyde Park Hotel, '72—followed by six months in the City (financial district) and a brief spell in a luggage factory on the Blackhorse Road before joining the army.

†Though there was no professional relationship between them as far as I'm aware (I had thought there was), Paul Cook introduced me to Mrs Lomax in 1971, and she, Rosemary*, offered me an apprenticeship to train as a jockey at her stables in Wiltshire. But, for reasons that were not expanded on at the time, she subsequently wrote that she could no longer take me on. I later learned that she and her husband, England cricketer Ian Lomax, had separated, but I cannot be certain that's why a career as an equestrian didn't materialise for me. C'est la vie.

†It troubles me, so I must mention it. For many years, I thought Mrs Lomax's name was Irene. I'm not at all sure why, can only surmise that I read: I. Lomax somewhere. Maybe the letter that I received was from her husband (They were a partnership). It's weak, I know, but it's all I have. It was about this time, at age 16, that I spent a weekend on Dartmoor with my Dad's TA Unit (His last posting—Romford, if my memory serves me right), helping me decide whether or not to enlist. It transpired that they wouldn't take me because I wasn't quite tall enough, and I had to return the following year.

From Nottinghamshire, I have been a Nottingham Forest fan since I was nine years old, when we returned to England from Tripoli, living with mum's parents in Newark (My birthplace, hometown) for several months before moving on to a British Forces Post Office (BFPO) address, BAOR. My late uncle was in the Forest squad c. 1950 but gave up the game to start a family. He then ran a painting and decorating business with his younger brother, who played for Newark. For my sins, I subsequently briefly followed Manchester United (in Münster) because they were typically the only team on the radio on weekends while overseas.

Football was in my blood from a young age, and I was—at one point—taught and coached by the late great John Atyeo (Kingdown School, Warminster), who had played for Bristol City and England. Dogged by injury as a boy, however, a military doctor told me, when I was thirteen, not to play. Nonetheless, I had played in a junior league in West Germany, and subsequently five-a-side after school in East London (Supporting The Orient and Spurs locally). And I did go on to play in the army—after a brief spell at boxing*—(including representing the Corps in a World Cup Competition in Amsterdam). Later, approached by Alton Town FC in 1982 when playing for The Blues & Royals (RHG/D), but regrettably had to turn them down.

†SEME Flyweight Champion, 1973.

After time away from my unit (RAF Hospital), I was to be sent back to BAOR, where I played once for the then army champions before a surgeon told me I wasn't permitted to play, due to a patellectomy—in the weeks leading up to the Falklands crisis. Soon after, I was back in rehabilitation (BMH Iserlohn (1983)), then returned to the UK in 1984* to complete my service pending demob on medical grounds.

†In the summer of 1984, before I returned to the UK, I was commissioned to take photographs of the 700th Anniversary of the Pied Piper for the Royal Engineers Sapper Magazine, some of which were in the BAOR press 'The Echo'. It was a weekend—I lost a good friend (LCpl Colin—Benny—Bennet RE) to a road traffic accident on the Monday, on my 28th birthday as it happened—the day after I'd taken photographs of him for his wife and kids back home—a very sad time. I had also worked for the Services Sound & Vision Corporation (SSVC) spanning 1983–84, which made the German press, 2026 (It's a long story).

In more recent years, following demob in '86, I tried my hand at a few jobs, including lorry driver, chief storekeeper/buyer in the building industry; fully trained as a driving instructor, but took a job as a civil servant with the MoD for a couple of years. After a period of toil and struggle, taking time out to campaign for a Conservative MP during the '97 GE, which he won, despite a nationwide surrender to Labour, I returned to college to study and became a part-time teacher; soon after, I was engaged as a data analyst (Powerdata), before embarking on two decades of self-employment in computer tech and small business consultancies.

My work included computer repair and design; periods in education, taking time out too, to train in educational consultancy; a salary position as a distance learning tutor (Became DELS) and a teaching contract as a lecturer in computer science. Then, following time in Surrey, a photographic editor and a contract with BT* (Global Services) as a computer skills, broadband and vision engineer (salary).

†Computers skills; assisting BT with the transition for BT Vision & Computer Skills.

For my final six years before retirement, though I continued to support small enterprises and my ageing broadband and computer client base, as I found it increasingly difficult to climb ladders and squat down on the floor, I became an ancillary vintage dealer and restorer, primarily restoring vintage GPO telephones. I maintain an interest in all things vintage, including telephones and books.

Family
Displaced due to military service, we're a somewhat distant, if not dysfunctional, family. My older brother, Chris—who alas I now seldom see—was a £10 pom. He later returned to the UK, ultimately to London (where we lived when I enlisted in '73). Stability has been kind to him, whereas I, having already been to eleven schools spanning ten years in three countries, embedded and travelled with the army from seventeen until shortly after my thirtieth birthday.

After Australia, Chris initially worked in theatre (Bournemouth Pier), later formed a company called Stageplan (not current), embarked on several new enterprises, including Bluw and brand consultancies; started a few different companies, founded the Karrot Group in 2006, Karrot Animation (2008) and is the co-owner of a now well-established animation studio in Central London. He is an executive producer of Peppa Pig and won a BAFTA for Sarah & Duck in 2014 (Pre-school)...

...I also have two sisters, one of whom lives in Australia. My youngest sister, Lynda, who has lived in Adelaide for some 35 years, was an extra in a movie (about a horse (I thought it was Black Beauty, but I can't make the dates work)); and when she was 18, she was a child's nanny for an actress who appeared in Doctor Who (as the Doctor's assistant). I'm not certain which one, but I believe it may have been Mary Tamm, who later sadly died of cancer.

Mum was from Newark, and Dad from Whitechapel, serving 22 years in the army—an engineer. His father had been a genuine East End rag'n bone man who reportedly served as an entertainer in the Great War. He died in 1964 (I saw him in 1962 before we embarked for North Africa). Through my father's family, I have a somewhat well-known relative (from Edmonton (Knighted)) who, sadly, doesn't know us. Dad told me that he last saw him c. 1949, when he was a young boy, when he—my dad—enlisted. Profile /End

Account Features
Brutal opinion; Cartoons; Classic ads; Coming soon to a channel near you; Foodie stuff; Illustrated journalism; In the News; Infrequent jokes; Life; Movie and TV clips; Occasional polls; On the grapevine; On the telly; Political humour; Politics and bad language; Small print; Sporadic music; Tomorrows Papers Today.

Politics 
Please be mindful, I tweet my mind. FSU Associate. No longer politically homeless (Crabby ex-Conservative member). I had been upbeat and optimistic for Reform*, nationally, but not bullish, as I do not agree with all aspects of Nigel's leadership and methodology—or Zia's seemingly mindless, if not damaging, obsession with the Tories; otherwise superb though he is—I appreciate their knowledge and insight, and like some of what they convey and stand for... 

...Individuals* can, of course, disagree. But to those who don't respect my right to an independent, multi-faceted opinion, however controversial, I bite back. I will remove followers I find remotely aggressive, offensive and/or unkind.

To my mind, †Reform banging on about the Tories is never-ending, exaggerated and boring—arguably disparaging from the otherwise well-intentioned Zia Yusuf, in an apparently relentless bid to undermine a political opponent. Most know who is behind the illegals invading our shores, i.e., from where the problem stems. Deflecting blame* for political gain will not resolve the problem.

†Absolution doesn't extend to the EU, a failed, arguably corrupt, concept that needs to be dismantled. It is possible to support Reform (Advance, Restore, for that matter) and have a common-sense, nationwide approach to voting. The numbers who force(d) blanket* views on others, to my mind, are damaging... 

...Come the general election, box clever, else Labour may still be in opposition, if not government—and they will disrupt, lie, undermine and subvert* in Parliament like they always have. Now that Restore has launched as a political party (February '26), I am fully on board with Rupert Lowe and a signed-up member (Day one). 

It strikes me as somewhat bizarre that Nigel, in recent weeks (August '26), labelled Restore 'far-right' in an apparent ongoing personal bid to redress historical accusations of racism. Meanwhile, at the same time, following a declaration from Nigel vis-á-vis pre-requisites for a collaboration between Reform and Restore, and the deletion of a grossly misleading article by GB News, Rupert Lowe said: "Restore Britain remains open to good faith talks where both parties understand the brutal electoral reality we are facing."

†In more recent months, whining about splitting the vote, to my mind, is a stark reminder why many of us have supported Rupert Lowe from the outset and/or more recently changed allegiance following the launch of Restore as a political movement in June 2025. Following Nigel's stance on the Portsmouth 'balaclava' gathering, it's apparent Reform may have lost a few more to Restore.

Splitting the Vote
Many seem to have forgotten that Starmer had such a large majority because of the reckless campaign by Nigel in 2024, standing candidates up and down the country that didn't show their face, let alone post a flyer. It ought to have been obvious when he repeatedly condemned the Conservatives after Labour won 63% of parliamentary seats, despite winning only 34% of the votes—"the lowest won by a post-war single party government".

Locally, we lost a good right-wing Conservative MP—who operated in the interests of our catchment area, remote from central government—by only 100 votes to the Labour candidate. The idea that that was a consequence of 'People being tired of the Tory Party' is another reason why I won't get behind Reform. 

Labour
†In 2017, more than 85% of Labour MPs stood on a platform for BREXIT under the pretence that they had accepted the outcome of the referendum—95% of their total number having earlier voted to REMAIN in the EU. 

The BBC later (in the early hours, after 2 am, on their 24-hour News channel) admitted to selecting Question Time panellists based on numbers standing on a platform for BREXIT in the wake of the result—encompassing the 85%-plus Labour MPs who largely voted to REMAIN in the EU but had stood on a platform for LEAVE following the referendum—ahead of the 2017 GE. Not on their political allegiance or how they had voted in 2016... 

...Following the 2017 GE, Labour, having deceived the electorate and cheated their way into Parliament, immediately set about subverting and disrupting, not least on the Borders Bill, which continued until 2019, if not the eve of Covid. 

Equilibrium 
Loyalist, and a designated OAP t'boot—supports remigration. At the height of the pandemic, I had covid and lived on savings—leading into retirement—for the best part of two years as self-employed work slowed, largely due to wider restrictions preventing me from visiting clients in their homes, which had been a significant part of my day-to-day commitment. Motorcycle accident in 2021 notwithstanding. 

Working from home, somewhat earlier, I stepped up on social media, mixing politics, in the run-up to and post-Brexit, with an ancillary* business account, increasingly supporting like-minded, notably relating to the 'state of the nation', but was ultimately suspended*—several times by the then Twitter admin... 

...I had a few goes at rebranding myself, including a dedicated (FactCheck) account focusing on Corbyn, circa 2017, his ambiguity and equivocation (his deception and misleading the listener), the myths and endless lies, which was shut down by Twitter faster than ..., well, faster than a Labour rat up their HQ drainpipe. Corbyn, of course, lost in 2017, but did better than expected. His results, however, were WORSE than those that led Brown to resign in 2010, but BETTER than those achieved by Starmer in 2024.

†Noted, early doors, for a spat with Stella Creasy, who accused me of being a 'racist white supremacist' (in a heated discussion with a grape farmer in Kent conceivably set to lose his EU funding) not simply for supporting Brexit, but for displaying a 1950s Hollywood poster of South African star Steve Reeves—The White Warrior—as my profile picture. She almost certainly didn't care that I was a supplementary vintage dealer with a respect for movie memorabilia.

†My existing X feed stems from that supplementary business account, which originally boasted some well-known and successful followers in the antiques trade—Of course, I sensed it slipping away as I became more political in the run-up to and following the referendum in 2016. I still have my main Twitter technical–business account from 2010, more recently renamed and redeployed.

†Little more than a year after Starmer lied to the nation for the keys to 10 Downing Street, as of September 2025, the Labour government's approval rating was down again from 13% to 11%, and Starmer's (Net) standing was at -59%. At the time of his resignation, I believe the party's national approval rating hovered close to 10%. That didn't stop him from addressing the country like we give a sh*t and fundamentally lying when suggesting he was leaving the UK in a better state than he found it — absolutely delusional.

Presently, I've toned it down, but occasionally swear (Due to time constraints, not limited capacity (Though short-term memory arguably a factor)). So, I'm sorry about that. I'm aware and strive to improve—always. The House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on South and Central Asia will hold an open hearing on Tuesday to investigate how nonprofits and activist networks may act as "Trojan horses" for foreign adversaries, reflecting a widening congressional crackdown on covert malign influence in the U.S.

The hearing, titled "Trojan Horses: Covert Foreign Malign Influence Operations in America," marks an expansion of congressional scrutiny beyond ongoing financial probes by the House Ways and Means Committee, which recently subpoenaed three nonprofits linked to American-born communist tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham.

Sam Lyman, head of research at the Bitcoin Policy Institute and a planned witness, warned that social media serves as a "gain-of-function for mind viruses" incubated overseas, heightening the threat of foreign influence in public discourse.

The panel is expected to examine influence campaigns stemming from China, Cuba, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and pro-Palestinian groups, assessing whether America’s open political system is being exploited to manipulate politics, public opinion, and strategic policy.

Mike Gonzalez, a senior fellow at the Heritage Foundation who will also testify, stated that adversaries like China and Cuba exploit America's open society to infiltrate sectors ranging from K-12 education and higher learning to government agencies and lobbying firms.

In March, Fox News Digital published an investigation tracking $591 million in transactions through the Singham network, detailing how Singham allegedly funneled $285 million into pro-China, pro-communist nonprofits like CodePink and the People's Forum starting in 2017.

The Justice Department is currently running a grand jury investigation into alleged financial crimes connected to Singham and these organizations; however, both have denied taking direction from the Chinese government, and no criminal charges have been filed.

The upcoming hearing aligns with the broader priorities of House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast, whose focus centers on confronting the Chinese Communist Party and strengthening U.S. defenses.

At the hearing, Gonzalez plans to focus on Cuba’s influence infrastructure in the U.S., describing the island nation as "ground zero for anti-American revolutionary organizing in the Western Hemisphere," while noting the significant overlap between Cuban support networks and the Singham network.

Another witness, Jamestown Foundation senior fellow Matthew Johnson, will offer expertise on the Chinese Communist Party’s strategic thinking, technology policy, and control over China's private economy.

Lyman will address campaigns targeting America's artificial-intelligence and data-center buildout, presenting research that links the Singham network and the Party for Socialism and Liberation to protests that have delayed or blocked an estimated $23.6 billion in proposed U.S. data-center investments.

Lyman noted that these disruptive domestic campaigns align with Chinese state media narratives criticizing American data centers, even as Beijing heavily subsidizes its own AI infrastructure expansion.

Meanwhile, House Ways and Means Chairman Jason Smith continues to investigate whether these tax-exempt groups are functioning as foreign agents, despite the organizations' refusal to comply with recent subpoenas, which they dismissed as a "witch hunt."

text:
THE U.S. JUST MADE A $16 BILLION BET ON NUCLEAR POWER

Amazon is backing nuclear energy as Big Tech races to secure electricity for AI data centers.

Amazon has committed up to $16 billion toward nuclear-powered data-center infrastructure in the United States.

The reason is simple: AI is creating an electricity demand shock.

A single hyperscale data center can require hundreds of megawatts of continuous power.

Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Meta are collectively spending hundreds of billions of dollars on AI infrastructure.

But building new gas plants, transmission lines and renewable projects takes time.

Nuclear offers something AI operators desperately need:

**24/7 electricity

high reliability

low carbon emissions

predictable power output**

The U.S. nuclear fleet currently has about 100 GW of operating capacity.

Now Big Tech wants a much larger share of that reliable power for the AI buildout.

The competition is shifting.

It is no longer just:

Who has the best AI model?

It is becoming:

Who can secure enough electricity to run it?

And Amazon's nuclear bet shows just how valuable reliable power could become in the AI economy.

text:
Once more into the ether.

When I was in a hospital bed waiting for an eventual stem cell transplant, I got in the habit of writing letters to my grandchildren. Here was one written with September 11 in mind.

Lest we forget…

Today is September 11. I remember where I was when we heard that John F Kennedy had been shot. I was home in New Glasgow. I certainly remember where I was when two planes crashed into the Twin Towers in New York. I was in my classroom but was not teaching that period. One of the teachers had a television as we were just into the new school with all the fancy tech hookups. Like many people, we were confused about the first strike, wondering if it could have been a weird accident, but the second attack fifteen minutes later revealed to all that this was terrorism. It was, to use an overworked word, surreal. After that came weeks of commentary.

Today I watched loved ones read out the names of those who died that day. Amazingly, it did not take long after the attack for some people to concoct crazy theories – the Jews did it was one; also, the government did it so they could conduct a war on terror. Others argued that America had it coming to them for being such a bully on the world stage. Conspiring with evil is never a pretty sight. These same people are with us today, still offering twisted interpretations that seek to justify evil.

I am pleased to see these rituals that ask us to keep alive the memory of what happened. I was astonished when I was in Cambodia a few years ago to hear that so few young people knew about their recent violent history where 2 million Cambodians were killed by the Khmer Rouge. We were told they were not interested. With so many pleasant distractions available on the internet, on television, and with the need to keep up with the social trends, who has time for the past? Well, of course, the real problem with that is this old saying: “Those who forget the past are doomed to repeat it.” Unfortunately, we may be doomed even if we do remember the past, but at least we give ourselves a chance to forestall it.

There is a grotesque number of evil events that took place in the 20th century that need to be continually refreshed and remembered.
The Soviet Union’s starvation of up to 7 million Ukrainians (called the Holodomor) and the many millions more in the Soviet gulags.
The genocide of 6 million Jews (and many hundreds of thousands of other minorities) by the Nazis.
The 45 million killed by Mao Tse Tung in his horrifying “Cultural Revolution” and “Great Leap Forward” in China.
The Cambodian nightmare conducted by Pol Pot.
The Turkish genocide of 2 million Armenians.
The genocide in Rwanda of up to 2 million Tutsis by the Hutus, their fellow countrymen.

The three thousand who died in the Twin Tower attacks seem a tiny number compared to the big events. But they all have something in common – they were caused by evil, a word not much in fashion these days.

We live in an age where there are no secrets. If you want to know about a subject, you need only consult google. Yet, the levels of ignorance concerning important events such as those listed above, is abysmal and shocking. The trouble is that we are distracted by the trivial and that pushes out the serious. We live in what some call a “celebrity culture” where what a celebrity had for breakfast, or who a celebrity is dating, or the ability of an athlete to hit or kick or catch a ball, dominates. What should be a passing interest becomes all-encompassing obsession. Who needs bad news when you can pull the covers over your head and pretend the world is just a jolly place of fame and fortune?

I gave ---- a thin book by George Orwell when she left Amherst. It is essential reading – "Animal Farm". It is an allegory, told through a farmyard of talking animals, for how totalitarian governments are born. These are the governments that perpetrated most of the list I gave above. The same writer wrote "1984", a more elaborate telling of the same theme. Both books should be read by anyone claiming to be educated.

“Lest we forget” is a bit ironic because too many have never heard of these too recent horrors. You can’t forget what you never knew.

The world is a wonderful place, (“just the right place for love, I don’t know where it’s like to go better” says the poet Robert Frost). I never doubted this, but this last year, where I did not always know how much more of life I was going to get, has made me appreciate even more the beauty and joy that life has to offer. Nonetheless, as adults, which you four are in the process of becoming, it is crucial that we understand the whole story of life: Siddhartha Gautama the Buddha and Adolf Hitler were both human and show the ends to which we can reach. As the ancient Greeks wisely said: Know thyself.

text:
THE PARABLE OF THE PLUCKED CHICKEN A Bible Study on Dependency, Power, Debt, and True Compassion
By Francis Gauthier
The “plucked chicken” story is often attributed to Joseph Stalin, but there is no reliable evidence that Stalin actually performed or told it. It should be understood as a political parable, not documented history.
Nevertheless, the warning behind it is worth examining.
A ruler strips a chicken of its feathers, leaving it wounded, frightened, and unable to protect itself. Then he scatters a few kernels of grain. The desperate bird follows the very hand that injured it because that hand now controls its relief.
The lesson is blunt: A government—or any powerful institution—can weaken people, make them dependent, and then demand gratitude for returning a fraction of what it took.
But does the Bible address this kind of manipulation?
It certainly does.
⸻
1. Debt Can Become a Chain
“The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.”
—Proverbs 22:7
This verse does not say every loan is sinful. It states an economic fact: the person who controls the money usually holds power over the person who needs it.
That applies to individuals, businesses, and nations.
When people become buried under debt, they lose choices. When a country spends money it does not have, its citizens eventually pay through higher taxes, inflation, reduced services, or a weakened currency. The bill may arrive years later, but the bill always arrives. Arithmetic remains stubbornly immune to campaign speeches.
Cross-references
“Owe no man any thing, but to love one another.”
—Romans 13:8
“The wicked borroweth, and payeth not again.”
—Psalm 37:21
“For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?”
—Luke 14:28
Jesus taught people to count the cost before beginning a project. That is basic wisdom for a household budget, a town budget, or a national budget.
Borrowing tomorrow’s money to buy today’s political applause is not compassion. It is passing the invoice to children who were not old enough to object.
⸻
2. Scripture Warns About Government Taking Too Much
When Israel demanded a king “like all the nations,” God instructed Samuel to warn the people about concentrated political power.
“He will take your sons, and appoint them for himself…”
—1 Samuel 8:11
“He will take your daughters…”
—1 Samuel 8:13
“He will take the tenth of your seed, and of your vineyards…”
—1 Samuel 8:15
“He will take the tenth of your sheep: and ye shall be his servants.”
—1 Samuel 8:17
Notice the repeated phrase: “He will take.”
God was not saying that all government is evil. Scripture recognizes legitimate civil authority. The warning was about giving rulers enough power to dominate the people they were supposed to serve.
Israel wanted security. It wanted a king who would solve its problems and fight its battles. God warned that the promised security would come with a price: property, labor, children, wealth, and eventually freedom.
That is the chicken parable in biblical terms. People surrender responsibility in exchange for promised protection, only to discover that the protector has become their master.
Cross-references
“Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of man, in whom there is no help.”
—Psalm 146:3
“It is better to trust in the LORD than to put confidence in princes.”
—Psalm 118:9
Government has a proper job, but government makes a miserable god. It cannot save the soul, manufacture virtue, or repeal the consequences of bad decisions.
⸻
3. God Condemns Leaders Who Feed Themselves
“Woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks?”
—Ezekiel 34:2
The leaders of Israel were called shepherds because they were supposed to protect and guide the people. Instead, they used their positions for personal advantage.
“Ye eat the fat, and ye clothe you with the wool, ye kill them that are fed: but ye feed not the flock.”
—Ezekiel 34:3
These leaders lived well while the people suffered. They consumed the flock instead of caring for it.
The same principle applies today. Public officials are supposed to be servants, not masters. Taxes are collected for legitimate public purposes—not to finance political machines, favored insiders, vanity projects, or permanent bureaucracies that exist mainly to justify their own budgets.
When leaders help create hardship and then present themselves as the only possible rescuers, something has gone badly wrong.
Cross-references
“Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, and that write grievousness which they have prescribed.”
—Isaiah 10:1
“The prince asketh, and the judge asketh for a reward; and the great man, he uttereth his mischievous desire.”
—Micah 7:3
“Thy princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves: every one loveth gifts, and followeth after rewards.”
—Isaiah 1:23
God does not excuse corruption because the guilty party holds an important title. A crooked ruler remains crooked even when the crookedness comes printed on official letterhead.
⸻
4. Returning What Was Taken Is Not Generosity
Suppose a man takes $100 from his neighbor, returns $10, and demands applause for his charity. Nobody would call that generosity.
Yet political systems sometimes operate through the same illusion. Government taxes wages, increases fees, borrows heavily, distorts markets, and piles regulatory costs onto ordinary goods. Then officials distribute a small benefit and expect people to treat it as a personal gift.
But government produces no wealth on its own. Every public dollar first comes from a taxpayer, a fee payer, or borrowed money that future taxpayers must repay.
This does not mean every public program is wrong. Roads, courts, police protection, national defense, and other legitimate functions require funding. The biblical question is whether authority is being exercised justly, honestly, and within proper limits.
“A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.”
—Proverbs 11:1
God cares about honest scales, honest money, honest contracts, and honest accounting. Moving numbers between columns does not create wealth. Renaming spending does not erase its cost.
⸻
5. Biblical Compassion Strengthens People
Here we must draw an important distinction.
The Bible repeatedly commands us to help the poor, the widow, the orphan, the stranger, the sick, and the person struck by genuine misfortune.
“He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD.”
—Proverbs 19:17
“Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.”
—Galatians 6:2
“I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink.”
—Matthew 25:35
The Bible does not teach cold-heartedness. It teaches active generosity.
But biblical compassion seeks to restore people, not trap them. It helps a man stand again. It does not break his legs and hand him a government-issued crutch.
The Good Samaritan used his own oil, wine, animal, time, and money to help a wounded stranger. He did not rob the next traveler and call the proceeds charity.
“But a certain Samaritan…had compassion on him.”
—Luke 10:33
True charity is personal, accountable, and directed toward an actual need. It sees the suffering person as a neighbor—not a voting bloc, a statistic, or a permanent client.
⸻
6. The Bible Balances Assistance With Responsibility
Scripture commands believers to help those who cannot provide for themselves. It also warns against encouraging deliberate idleness.
“For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat.”
—2 Thessalonians 3:10
Paul did not say that someone who cannot work should be abandoned. He spoke about someone who would not work.
That distinction matters.
“But if any provide not for his own…he hath denied the faith.”
—1 Timothy 5:8
“Let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth.”
—Ephesians 4:28
The biblical pattern is productive and dignified:
1. Work when you are able.
2. Provide for your household.
3. Save wisely.
4. Help those facing genuine need.
5. Restore the struggling person to stability when possible.
Good assistance becomes a bridge back to independence. Bad assistance becomes a toll road with no exit.
⸻
7. Fear Is One of the Oldest Tools of Control
In the parable, the chicken follows because it is wounded and afraid.
Fear narrows a person’s thinking. A frightened population may surrender freedoms it would never surrender in calmer times. People begin asking, “Who will take care of me?” instead of, “What power am I giving away?”
“The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe.”
—Proverbs 29:25
“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.”
—2 Timothy 1:7
A sound mind asks questions:
* Who created this crisis?
* Who benefits from the proposed solution?
* What will this program cost?
* Who will pay for it?
* Does the program solve the problem or enlarge the bureaucracy?
* Does the help restore independence or reward permanent dependence?
* What freedom must be surrendered in exchange?
Those are not cruel questions. They are the questions responsible citizens should ask before handing anyone more power.
⸻
8. Civil Government Has a Legitimate—but Limited—Role
The Bible does not teach anarchy.
“For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil.”
—Romans 13:3
“For he is the minister of God to thee for good.”
—Romans 13:4
Government should punish wrongdoing, protect the innocent, maintain public order, and administer justice impartially.
But Romans 13 does not turn every government decision into the will of God. The same Bible records faithful people resisting rulers who commanded evil.
“We ought to obey God rather than men.”
—Acts 5:29
“And the king of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwives…But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them.”
—Exodus 1:15,17
Government deserves lawful respect, but it does not deserve worship, blind obedience, or unlimited power. Caesar has a proper place. Caesar does not own everything.
“Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar’s; and unto God the things that are God’s.”
—Matthew 22:21
⸻
9. Freedom Requires Self-Government
Political freedom cannot survive long among people who refuse to govern themselves.
“He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.”
—Proverbs 25:28
A free society depends on people who work, save, keep their word, raise their children, help their neighbors, restrain their appetites, and accept responsibility for their decisions.
When families, churches, neighborhoods, and local communities abandon these duties, government rushes into the empty space. Sometimes it comes with good intentions. Sometimes it comes looking for power. Usually it brings paperwork.
The strongest defense against unhealthy dependence is not selfishness. It is responsible independence joined with voluntary generosity.
“Study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands.”
—1 Thessalonians 4:11
“For every man shall bear his own burden.”
—Galatians 6:5
Galatians tells us both to “bear one another’s burdens” and to “bear [our] own burden.” That is not a contradiction. We should carry our normal responsibilities while helping neighbors overwhelmed by loads they cannot carry alone.
That is biblical balance: responsibility without hardness, compassion without manipulation.
⸻
10. How Do We Keep From Following the Grain Into the Cage?
Work and prepare
“The hand of the diligent shall bear rule: but the slothful shall be under tribute.”
—Proverbs 12:24
Develop useful skills. Reduce unnecessary debt. Save what you can. Maintain your home, tools, health, and relationships. Prepared people are harder to frighten and harder to control.
Practice private generosity
“God loveth a cheerful giver.”
—2 Corinthians 9:7
Help through families, churches, food pantries, community organizations, and direct neighbor-to-neighbor action. Charity works best when it includes human contact and accountability.
Demand honest government
“He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God.”
—2 Samuel 23:3
Read budgets. Request records. Attend meetings. Question debt. Examine contracts. Follow the money. Public money should withstand public inspection.
Refuse political idolatry
No party, politician, or agency can replace God, family, church, and community. Support what is right. Oppose what is wrong. Never surrender your conscience to a party label.
Tell the truth
“Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour.”
—Ephesians 4:25
Do not exaggerate to make a political point. The truth is strong enough to stand without counterfeit evidence. That is why the chicken story must be identified as a parable rather than passed around as verified history.
⸻
Final Lesson
The plucked chicken represents a person stripped of security, independence, and confidence. The grain represents a small benefit offered by the same power that helped create the suffering. The cage represents the final destination of unchecked dependency.
But the Christian answer is not to despise the poor or refuse help to the hurting. It is to build a society in which people can work, own property, raise families, practice faith, help neighbors, and live without constantly begging distant officials for permission or relief.
Government should protect liberty and administer justice. Families should care for their own. Churches should serve the vulnerable. Citizens should work, prepare, give, and remain watchful.
Never confuse control with compassion.
Never mistake a political allowance for personal freedom.
And never become so grateful for a few kernels that you forget who removed the feathers.
Biblical principle: “Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free” (Galatians 5:1). Use freedom responsibly, help your neighbor willingly, and never trade God-given stewardship for a comfortable cage.

In the early 1990s I started an Internet service provider called NetWave in Chicago.  It was the second ISP to provide Internet access in the Chicagoland area.

I started with a Linux box with 4 x 14.4 kbps modems attached to it (with a Cyclades multiport card), and an Ascend Pipeline router with a 64K connection to a large telco for backbone.

I started by putting fliers in every home around my neighborhood.   For every 100 fliers I would get 10 signups at $19.95 per month.

4 modems turned into 8 ... then 16 ... then the Telco said they could NOT put more lines in my house.

I took an office downtown Chicago to get more lines and eventually colocated with MCI-Worldcom at their facilities in the Prudential Plaza.  Colocated with Level3 at their data centers ... and rented space in the Sears Tower, CBOT building, and Prudential Plaza.

My customers at those buildings were Nations Bank, Merrill Lynch,  Latham and Watkins ... Motorola ... the biggest US corporations... selling them 10 mbps service for $1500 per month.  Ethernetix was the name of the in-building service.

I became a CLEC in Illinois (competitive local exchange carrier) and offered DSL services nationwide thru Rythms.

The person that managed the risers in the Sears Tower was a consultant at the Twin Towers in NYC.  He said he would take me there to become a provider in those buildings.  I was also negotiating to colocate antenas at the top of the Sears Tower for using 802.11b horizontally into adjacent buildings.

Then Sept 11 happened.  I was driving towards my office in the Sears Tower and heard the news on the radio.  Turned back home ... saw it on TV.

After that, everything changed.  Tenants started leaving the big buildings in Chicago.  I lost 1/2 my customers.  Had to take my company bankrupt because of it.

From 4 modems in the basement of my house, to the top of the world, then back to nothing.

Life has its ups and downs and sometimes you have no control.

But I am a persistent person and I am starting again ... this time is Siguimi.  

Started with 0 ... let's see how far I can get.

text:
It's worth recalling in this regard that one of the possible boundary lines offered by the American party to the conference negotiating the end to the Revolutionary War (in addition to the frontier that now exists) was for the Canada-U.S. line to follow the 45th parallel—which now makes the northern frontier of New York state with Canada.

If that proposal had been adopted, continuing that 45° boundary line to the west, the present deep plunge by Canada into the U.S. wouldn't exist.

Moreover, if that 45° (halfway to the pole) line had been followed all the way across America, the U.S.-Canada frontier would follow what's now the southern border of Montana (almost completely eliminating that state from the Union); thereupon splitting Idaho and Oregon down the middle—discarding in the West almost the entire Columbia River drainage along with the whole state of Washington—not to speak of all of North Dakota and most of Minnesota, Wisconsin, and Michigan in the East—from the Union. But today's southeastern Ontario would be in the U.S.

Interesting to think how that might have changed subsequent history—such as the War of 1812, and beyond.

Both. W.E.B. Du Bois was a towering, polarizing figure whose reception shifted sharply over his 95-year life (1868–1963). He was widely respected as a scholar and civil-rights leader for decades, then increasingly isolated, attacked, and treated as a pariah in his final years. 
Celebrated as an intellectual and activist
Du Bois was the first African American to earn a PhD from Harvard. His 1903 book The Souls of Black Folk became a landmark, introducing ideas like “double consciousness” and declaring that “the problem of the twentieth century is the problem of the color line.” It polarized readers at the time—some white reviewers rejected its critique of racism, and some Black readers were unsettled by its attack on Booker T. Washington’s accommodationist strategy—but it established him as a leading voice among Black intellectuals and progressives. 
He helped found the Niagara Movement and the NAACP, and as editor of The Crisis (1910–1934) he reached a large audience (circulation peaked around 100,000). He was a central organizer of Pan-African Congresses and produced pioneering scholarship, including The Philadelphia Negro and later Black Reconstruction in America (1935). For much of the early-to-mid 20th century he was regarded as the preeminent Black protest leader and public intellectual in the United States. 
Opposed and later persecuted
Du Bois’s opposition to Booker T. Washington split Black leadership into “radical” and “conservative” camps. His later leftward turn—sympathy for socialism, praise for the Soviet Union and China, and criticism of U.S. imperialism and the Cold War—made him a target.
During the McCarthy era he was investigated by the FBI, indicted in 1951 as an unregistered foreign agent for circulating an anti-nuclear petition through the Peace Information Center, and put on trial. He was acquitted for lack of evidence, but the publicity wrecked his career, isolated him from the mainstream civil-rights movement (the NAACP distanced itself), and led the State Department to revoke his passport from 1952 to 1958. 
In 1961 he formally joined the Communist Party, moved to Ghana at Kwame Nkrumah’s invitation, and became a Ghanaian citizen. He died there on August 27, 1963—the day before the March on Washington. At the time of his death he was viewed as a pariah by the U.S. establishment and, to a degree, by some civil-rights leaders; Roy Wilkins of the NAACP offered only a brief, reluctant tribute at the March. 
His reputation recovered and grew substantially after his death. During his lifetime the pattern was celebration mixed with controversy that, in his last decade, turned into official hostility and isolation.

Acoustic Psycho-Correction. So-called Russian Mind Control. In 1993, two or three articles appeared describing Russians interfacing with Americans on the question of mind control. APC is not what you think. It’s more like subliminal audio. The Soviets were using it in the 80s to alleviate guilt of SPEZNAZ over killing women and children in Afghanistan. CIA acquired it in the 80s. I have no idea how effective it is at getting people to do things they don’t want to do. Gonna guess not very. But if you’re suffering with guilt, maybe it helps.

OR, if you really, really, really already wanna strike out at “the Great Satan,” maybe it can tell you HOW to do so.

Two articles, the most detailed, are from Defense News and Defense Electonics.

Clinton had Presidential inquiries into claims of various human experimentation programs and apologized to the victims publicly. The hearings only went up to a point in the 1970s but may have been prompted by something more recent. Anyway, this is likely why those articles appeared when they did.

The next one involves understanding proxy wars and proxy terror. Let me begin with Operation: Gladio. The idea was that post WWII, NATO set up networks in place to help repel any Soviet invasion of Europe; failing that, behaving as the French Underground to undermine the control of whatever regions that they invaded. It was created by James Bond creator Ian Fleming’s brother who, like Fleming, was British Intelligence. The Soviet invasion never happened but Gladio went on to do other things. Reportedly it sometimes ran IRA operations in order to turn British public opinion against the IRA and to slow down or prevent Irish independence. Similarly, once in a while it was responsible for far left terror attacks in Italy for much the same reason. Socialist parties were gaining popularity and so they did those false flags in order undermine that popularity. Both of those operations worked for a time.

Of course most people are familiar with the US and the USSR using different groups, tribes, of mujahideen against each other in Afghanistan. CIA trained some and the Soviets others. On 9/11, in a sort of similar move, Bin Laden had his rivals killed so they would be unable to help the US hunt him down.

The one that interests me most though was the Red Brigade. Red Brigade was a Communist terror group operating out of East Germany during the Cold War, while Germany was still split. It conducted attacks in West Germany aimed at night clubs where Americans frequented. They accepted responsibility and for decades that was the story.

More recently, I believe from Catherine Belton interviewing former Red Brigade members, it was discovered that not only was the East German secret police involved in the planning and other aspects of the attacks, which came as little surprise, but so was the Russian KGB. That was perhaps a bit more surprising. At least the American people knew nothing of it even if CIA, NSA or FBI knew earlier.

But do you see the point there? In all of these really. The IRA wanted to attack English interests. The Red Brigade wanted to attack American interests. Neither of those NEEDED anything else to make them a whole story. And yet both did have more to the story. It wasn’t just the desire to use terror to try to get a political goal; it was other entities with similar but ultimately different agendas (in Gladio, the complete opposite by leveraging the public outcry). KGB attacked the United States but kept their involvement a secret and it happened when, where and how because of them, even though the Red Brigade would have liked to have done something on their own.

The point: It can be Al Qaeda in the planes. They can absolutely want the US out of the Middle East. They don’t even have to know that there’s anyone else involved. In fact, I’m not sure they did. That’s where the acoustic psycho-correction comes in.

When the US invaded Afghanistan and started following Bin Laden’s trail, they came upon some home videos a man had made when he was hosting Bin Laden some days after the attacks. Though Bin Laden doesn’t come out and say he planned it, funded it, pulled it off, what he does say is incredibly interesting. He mentions a man that both he and the host know who was having dreams. And Bin Laden said if his dreams had been any closer to the truth, he would have had to kill him.

First, the clearly shows foreknowledge. Ie, they did it.

But how do you explain the man with the dreams?

What if, and there are holes here. Would it be SVR or GRU? Gonna guess SVR.

But what if they were feeding Bin Laden and other leaders the planning and ideas for the attacks via acoustic psycho-correction, that is just plain old subliminal audio over, say, radio and television in Afghanistan? It would explain a great number of things.

Though I don’t know for certain it’s true, it seemed as if Bin Laden didn’t care for Russian presence in Afghanistan and the Middle East much either. This would have gotten around that problem. Though it’s likely, if this scenario is true, that they had their men inside anyway.

In Bill Clinton’s famous interview on FOX News where he is questioned about chasing Bin Laden and so on, the one where he gets emphatic and bit upset and pushes back, he mentions that the 9/11 Commission Report is itself a political document. He means it has biases.

I don’t want to get too far off track here but a few things do stand out about the report. The word Russia does not appear in the Index. Sons of the people involved may have also been involved in the network that sold nuclear secrets to Israel. Much like what we’re talking about here, I don’t think that was official US policy. But I do think, once it was done, authorities preferred to keep it quiet and let it go rather than punish the rogue Congressmen and other officials involved. It was mostly Republicans but there were a few Democrats involved also. The main problem is, they were sold through Turkey and somewhere along the pipeline the documents may have been copied and sold to, now deceased, but then infamous international arms dealer A.Q. Khan.

Another thing that must be mentioned is the beheading event and video of WSJ reporter Daniel Pearl. In the video one can plainly see the arm of one of the men is white, not someone from the desert, and Russian language can be heard being spoken in the background, possibly the “director” of the video.

Next, when a certain Russian businessman (some say Russian mob connected) was up on stock fraud charges by DoJ in 1999, just two years prior to 9/11, he offered access to Russian intelligence networks in Afghanistan as related to watching Al Qaeda specifically. This means that post-Soviet Russian intelligence was still connected inside Afghanistan despite having lost “Charlie Wilson’s War,” essentially going broke and collapsing from trying to wage a war there. Of course articles don’t say what happened but I’m pretty sure his stay in prison was short one.

But the word Russia doesn’t appear in the Index of the 9/11 Commission Report.

Back to my pinned tweet for a second. FBI was known to have looked at Giuliani’s Russian backers. A lot of people only know him as far back as the former Mayor of New York. He worked for Reagan’s Department of Justice and is often partially credited with pushing the Italian mob out of New York and in some cases into prison. But this is the odd part, right? Why does that guy have Russian mob backing his campaigns for Mayor of New York in the 90s? Because by pushing out the Italians, he made room for the Russians. And the main difference is the former protected the unions and the latter do not.

I remind folks here that Reagan considered unions evil and broke some of them, started that move. It was a goal of the GOP. And this is my main (apart from the personal ones involving Charles McGonigal and so forth) beef with FBI. While sure we care about organized crime, if it’s a net zero and we not only killed labor but gave a hostile foreign nation a foot in the door, then that goes way beyond mere law enforcement. It’s a purposeful undermining of both the middle class and democracy as a whole. We are in part because of the wealth gap. There are only so many way to counteract that.

And so we’re at the point where we have to ask who knew? There is of course Buzzy Krongard’s two bizarre things. The first, he spent the Summer of 2001 frantically making sure the fire alarm and sprinkler systems at CIA was working. The second, the trading company where he worked just prior to returning to CIA was one of the ones that had the attempts at short selling airline stocks on 9/11.

That does not make it an “inside job” necessarily, whatever it is that that phrase is supposed to mean. It does look like rogue elements again, as with the nuclear secrets situation.

There are other things, like Tenet’s scheduled absence from the CIA HQ. But don’t see why that cannot be coincidence. You’d have to know how often he’s there and how often he’s interfacing outside to do the odds on that and we don’t have the information.

But what we see is, it shook things up. It paved the way for Trump, really. As it had prior paved the way for Rudy but that failed. In part over a phone call.

—

As for why I’m doing this, when clearly it’s not a healthy thing to do. Well they know why. I spent most of Thursday morning and afternoon at a courthouse. I’ve already said most of it and don’t care to repeat it here. I’ve said why it’s not effective means of shutting me up. Yet, they persist.

There’s probably more I’ll think of later and add. Probably should say something about McGonigal. I had no idea he ran the Wikileaks and Illegals investigations from DC before going to NYC, but that certainly helped solidify a few things. Maybe, just maybe, FBI didn’t really intend, any more than Ronald Reagan did with his tax cuts for the top, to destroy democracy and the United States. Still not a great situation, but also not as bad as it could be.

I’ve also been told that none of this matters any more. That’s pretty damn dark. Why would that be?

Happy Friday, if you can.

text:
Philip, not Stephen. Stephen was stoned a chapter earlier…

Setting that aside, you just made my argument. Baptism and the laying on of hands are distinct acts, the laying on of hands confers the Holy Ghost, and a higher authority is required for it. That is our position exactly.

I'd only add that Philip was not a passerby either. He was one of the Seven, and Acts 6:6 says the apostles prayed and laid their hands on them. The man doing the baptizing in Acts 8 had himself been ordained. He simply held a lesser priesthood than Peter and John held. Two levels of conferred authority, not one conferred and one open to anyone.

"Anyone" cannot baptize.

When Jerusalem sent priests and Levites to the Jordan, they never asked whether baptizing was permitted. They asked what office he held. Art thou the Christ? Elijah? That prophet? He denies all three, and then comes the question: "Why baptizest thou then, if thou be not that Christ, nor Elias, neither that prophet?"

They assumed the right to do this belonged to someone in particular.

Then Christ makes baptism the test. Pressed in the temple, "By what authority doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authority?" He answers with a question of His own: "The baptism of John, whence was it? from heaven, or of men?"

Notice what both questions assume. Theirs, that authority is given by someone. His, that baptism was authorized by someone. From heaven, or from men. Either God commissioned John, or John took it up himself. No third possibility is offered.

That question cannot be asked about something anyone can do.

And Luke says the Pharisees, "being not baptized of him," rejected the counsel of God. The Greek is atheteo, a legal term for annulling a covenant, paired with boule, the settled purpose of God. They voided God's purpose toward themselves by declining an ordinance at the hands of the very man who held it.

That’s not the language someone uses about an ordinance requiring no one in particular.

We agree that authority is required. The only question left is who holds it now, and how they came by it.

I've been putting actual dates on this thesis for a while, so before moving the goalposts after the fact, here's what has lined up so far.

WHAT I ACTUALLY CALLED
============================

✓ Earnings around Sept. 8-10. They landed Sept. 8. Not exactly the hardest prediction in the world, but important because I expected earnings to fall directly inside the start of the settlement window.

✓ Positive price action beginning around Sept. 8/9. GME traded into the high $17s and has now pushed back through $21.

So far, the first part has shown up. I was hoping for an eBay presentation which may be pending.

I'm also not pretending $17 → $21 is some historic GME breakout. We've spent plenty of time above $24 over the last several years.

The point is that the move is happening in the window I was watching, while several other pieces of the thesis are starting to line up.

THE FRACTAL
============================

==] 2020 [==

Ryan Cohen began accumulating actual GME shares aggressively in August. This aligns with our current price action; the MACD from that spring and summer align very well. Breakout took about 4 weeks to transpire though.

GameStop itself wasn't remotely as financially prepared as it is today, but it ultimately used the improving market conditions to raise equity and clean up longer-term debt in 2021.

There are also some interesting Obligation Warehouse RECAPS overlaps:

• Aug. 28 RECAPS → Aug. 31 settlement, during Cohen's August accumulation. 8/31/20 was a massive day.

• Oct. 14 RECAPS → Oct. 15 settlement. GME had another unusually high-volume positive session on Oct. 15.

• Jan. 13, 2021 RECAPS → Jan. 14 settlement. Enough said.

• Jan. 28 RECAPS → Jan. 29 settlement occurred directly inside the peak volatility.

That does NOT mean RECAPS caused any of those moves. There were other RECAPS dates that produced nothing useful. I view it as a recurring timing variable worth monitoring, not some hidden mandatory squeeze clock.

==] 2024 [==

The April/May sequence is arguably even more interesting.

• Apr. 25 RECAPS → Apr. 26 settlement occurred right around the turn out of the April lows. GME then began climbing into early May.

• May 9 RECAPS → May 10 settlement occurred immediately before Keith Gill publicly.

Again, the important part is that GME was ALREADY moving before the obvious public catalyst appeared.

Somebody was buying.

We later learned Gill had accumulated an enormous common/options position, although the public record doesn't let us perfectly reconstruct every purchase date.

GameStop was also much more prepared in 2024. When the volatility arrived, the company used it to raise billions of dollars.

==] 2026 [==

Now we have another depressed GME valuation followed by concentrated buying and a possible early re-rating.

The warrants actually moved aggressively BEFORE the common did much, which was one of the first things that caught my attention.

Then:

• Aug. 31: GameStop terminates the remaining 35-trading-day convertible-exchange VWAP early and substitutes $358.4M of cash for additional equity consideration.

• Sept. 3: exchange closes and ~55.5M shares are delivered.

• Sept. 8: earnings + Cheng purchase.

• Sept. 9: additional insider buying.

• Sept. 10: Ryan Cohen buys another 1,000,000 GME shares.

Now GME is pushing $21+.

That doesn't tell us settlement pressure is causing the move. The insider purchases are obviously real demand and the filings themselves create additional demand because investors see management putting meaningful money behind the stock.

But the timing raises a more interesting possibility:

The exchange-related mechanism capable of creating additional hedge/sell supply stops, then concentrated long demand appears immediately afterward.

You don't necessarily need a gigantic forced-cover event.

Removing a persistent seller can make the next buyer matter a hell of a lot more.

RECAPS: THE NEXT DATE
============================

The current schedule gives us another interesting overlap:

• Sept. 17 RECAPS → Sept. 18 settlement (quarterly OpEx / quad witching).

That lands directly inside the window I've already been watching.

RECAPS reconfirms, reprices and renets eligible aged Obligation Warehouse positions at current market values. It is NOT a rule requiring every old GME obligation to suddenly be bought back.

But if meaningful obligations exist, repricing them becomes more interesting when the stock itself is moving rapidly higher.

My working timing remains:

Sept. 9 → Sept. 17: first leg / re-rating attempt

Sept. 18 → Sept. 22: potentially the strongest positive portion if momentum, options and settlement mechanics continue reinforcing each other

~Sept. 23: original reset / transition area from the thesis

That's roughly 11 trading sessions from Sept. 9 through Sept. 23.

Obviously that doesn't mean 11 green days. There will be resistance, volatility and probably some violent intraday reversals.

THE RE-RATING MATTERS TO GAMESTOP
============================

The latest SEC filings repeatedly describe GameStop's acquisition strategy around finding assets capable of a "significant re-rating under our stewardship."

Technically that language refers to assets GameStop wants to acquire, not GME itself.

But GME's own valuation is directly relevant to the proposed eBay transaction because roughly half of the consideration is supposed to be GameStop equity.

A higher GME price means fewer shares are needed to provide the stock consideration, less dilution, stronger acquisition currency and a more credible equity component for eBay shareholders.

Then there are ~59M warrants with a $32 strike.

If the common eventually trades sufficiently above $32 and warrant holders exercise, GameStop could receive roughly another $1.9B in cash.

So the company has an unusually strong incentive for the market to understand and properly value its equity, provided that value comes from legitimate operating, strategic and corporate developments.

2020: GameStop used the volatility while trying to stabilize its financial position.

2024: GameStop used the volatility to dramatically increase its capital base.

Today it has billions of liquidity, a $2B buyback authorization, ~59M warrants capable of providing another ~$1.9B, a 9.8% eBay stake and a proposed acquisition where GME stock itself is part of the consideration.

I've gone into all of that in previous posts.

SO WHAT PUSHES IT OVER THE EDGE?
============================

This is where the exact catalyst is unknowable.

The setup can develop first and the recognizable explanation can arrive later. That's arguably what happened in 2024.

A few things that would immediately get my attention:

• GameStop finally releases the detailed eBay investor presentation with financing, leverage, cost reductions, integration, governance and Cohen's $500M commitment explained.

• GameStop makes more definitive progress on the eBay proposal or eBay begins engaging.

• GameStop acquires additional eBay shares.

• Keith Gill reappears or another large entity starts accumulating GME common/options.

• A new investor files a meaningful 13D position in GME.

• The unexplained warrant accumulation resumes or we eventually learn a significant entity has been accumulating https://t.co/K2Ob88jpmT.

• GameStop deploys capital unexpectedly. A buyback would surprise me given the complications surrounding the eBay proposal, but the authorization exists and this company has made a habit of doing things the market wasn't expecting.

There are plenty of potential matches.

We don't know which one lights it. I would hope for multiple moving parts.

THE PART THAT WOULD BE MOST COMPELLING
============================

Imagine GME doesn't need the big catalyst yet.

Insider buying and whatever else is happening take it from ~$18 → $21 → $23-$25.

The option structure gets progressively more sensitive as additional strikes move toward/into the money. Warrants continue repricing. Sept. 17 RECAPS and Sept. 18 settlement/OpEx arrive while spot is already elevated.

Then, only once that setup has developed, GameStop just so happens to reach a legitimate point where it can release the eBay presentation, announce firmer financing, increase the eBay stake, advance the offer or disclose some other strategic development.

The same announcement hitting GME at $24-$28 would encounter a very different market than the same announcement hitting GME at $18.

And if that pushes GME toward $30-$32, the warrants stop looking like distant optionality and start becoming potential acquisition capital.

That's the feedback loop I've been discussing in the other thesis posts.

BOTTOM LINE
============================

I am not calling the breakout complete. We're at ~$21, not $30.

But quite a few pieces I expected to converge in September are now converging:

✓ Earnings Sept. 8

✓ Positive price action beginning around Sept. 8/9

✓ Convertible-exchange share calculation terminated before the window

✓ Exchange settlement completed Sept. 3

✓ Warrants repriced aggressively before the common

✓ Multiple insiders begin buying immediately afterward

✓ Cohen purchases another 1M shares

✓ Sept. 17 RECAPS → Sept. 18 settlement / quarterly OpEx still ahead

✓ Sept. 18-22 remains my highest-interest positive window

✓ ~Sept. 23 remains the reset/transition area from the original thesis

✓ The biggest potential corporate catalyst — meaningful progress on eBay — still hasn't shown itself

2020 had concentrated buying before the larger move.

2024 had concentrated buying and a re-rating before the obvious public catalyst.

2026 now has concentrated insider buying, strange warrant behavior, an unusual capital-structure setup and a stock beginning to re-rate directly inside the window I laid out beforehand.

If GME clears the old ~$24 area and does it before the next major buyer or corporate catalyst reveals itself, I think the 2020/2024 comparison becomes a lot harder to dismiss.

I still think Sept. 18-22 has the potential to be a big deal...

See my previous posts / Sept-Oct thesis for the convertible exchange, settlement, C+35, RECAPS, options, warrants and eBay mechanics behind this.

#threatreport:
The report describes two separate job-offer-themed malware campaigns that begin with archives containing files disguised as employment documents. Both require only a single user execution and then operate largely without further interaction, using decoys, in-memory execution, defense evasion, and Task Scheduler COM persistence. Campaign 1 is associated with a Vietnam-linked criminal cluster previously connected to PXA Stealer and PureRAT activity. Its recovered command-and-control infrastructure is 15.235.156.143 on ports 56001–56003.

Campaign 1 uses a ZIP archive containing a renamed, signed WinWord.exe and a malicious AppVIsvSubsystems64.dll for DLL side-loading. The DLL launches a portable Python runtime and a script disguised as update.dll. The loader removes Mark-of-the-Web indicators, displays a decoy document, hides staging files, and decrypts additional Python code from an XOR-encrypted file named support.ico. The payload uses base64, bzip2, zlib, and Python marshal serialization before executing Donut shellcode. Donut reflectively loads a .NET Reactor-protected PureRAT implant into memory.

The first campaign establishes persistence through Task Scheduler COM registration, a permanent WMI event subscription, and a per-user COM hijack targeting the MMDeviceEnumerator CLSID. It also maintains mirrored staging directories for self-recovery. AMSI and ETW are bypassed through hardware-breakpoint interception and direct patching of AmsiScanBuffer and EtwEventWrite. PureRAT communicates over TLS using a length-prefixed protobuf protocol with certificate pinning, profiles the host, searches Chromium-based browser profiles and desktop wallets, and supports plugins for keylogging, credential theft, clipboard manipulation, remote access, and code execution.

Campaign 2 uses a malicious LNK disguised as Job Interview.pdf to launch mshta.exe. The HTA downloads p.exe and an encrypted hda_config.dat while opening a blank PDF decoy. The loader reflectively maps a native DLL into memory and starts a worker thread. Its implant performs uptime, memory, disk, display, and host-specific delay checks to evade sandboxes, creates a persistent agent identity, profiles the host, and communicates through task-based C2 messages. Persistence is installed through Task Scheduler COM APIs using a disguised “Windows System Update Service” task with a logon trigger. No public overlap or attribution was identified for this campaign.

“Helping people... that's what's given me a lot of emotional body armor through the years.” 🚨

Marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11 terrorist attacks, retired Army Lt. Col. Ryan Yantis shared his powerful eyewitness account of surviving inside the Pentagon when hijacked American Airlines Flight 77 struck the building on September 11, 2001. 🇺🇸🪖

Inside the secure, windowless Army Operations Center, alarms suddenly pierced the silence as a security desk sergeant ordered everyone to evacuate.

But once outside the smoke-filled corridors, Yantis didn't simply flee. He grabbed an empty stretcher, returned toward the burning wreckage, and began helping carry the wounded to safety.

His story offers a profound lesson about resilience: sometimes, helping others can become a source of strength even while carrying your own wounds.

Yantis has also spoken openly about his ongoing experience with PTSD, using his story not only to honor those who were lost but also to encourage others facing deep adversity to look beyond themselves, serve others, and keep moving forward. 🛐🇺🇸🪖🗽✨

Fine for nearshore or bay runs. Avoid being caught in thunderstorms.

Fair to good nearshore with ~2 ft seas. Best clarity during slack tides. Storm chances present afternoon.

(Miami reference): As listed above — strong morning high and afternoon low offer solid windows. Light SE flow overlays tidal currents.

Slack periods ideal for diving. Fish early or late to avoid heat and storms. Gulf Stream edges productive offshore.

text:
Charlie Kirk didn’t have to be the first. He had an extraordinary ability to take something that already existed and make it better than ever.

Youth chapters existed before TPUSA. Conservative conferences existed before AmericaFest. Faith gatherings existed before TPUSA Faith. Political podcasts existed before The Charlie Kirk Show. Ballot chasing existed before Turning Point Action. Campus debates existed before “Prove Me Wrong.”

Charlie didn’t invent all of these things.

He mastered them.

Whatever arena he entered, Charlie studied it, improved it, modernized it, scaled it—and somehow, in category after category, became the best in the business.

He was one of the most intellectually gifted people I ever knew. His memory was extraordinary. He could absorb enormous amounts of information, recall facts seemingly on command, and communicate complicated ideas in a way anyone could understand.

To me, he was the best public speaker and debater in the movement. And nowhere was he more in his element than on a college campus. Put Charlie in front of students—especially students who disagreed with him—and he came alive. Whatever the question, he always seemed to have an answer.

Then there was Charlie the coalition builder.

MAGA and MAHA. Evangelicals and tech entrepreneurs. Neoconservatives and libertarians. Establishment Republicans and populists. Lifelong conservatives and former Democrats.

They didn’t agree on everything. Charlie knew they didn’t have to. He had a remarkable ability to find what united people, bring them into the same coalition, and hold that coalition together.

And behind all of that was Charlie the friend—and Charlie the Christian.

His faith wasn’t something reserved for the stage. In the mornings, as he read his Bible, Charlie would sometimes text Scriptures to friends and colleagues.

I was blessed to receive a couple of those texts.

My favorite was 2 Timothy 1:7:

“For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind.”

Looking back, I can’t think of a verse that better reflected the way Charlie tried to live his life.

One of my favorite memories is Charlie asking me why I wasn’t married yet. I’d tell him, “I just haven’t found the right one.”

He’d look out over the crowd at the Texas Youth Summit and say, “Look at all these women here. Just pick someone.”

I’d laugh.

Two months before his death, I saw Charlie at an event and finally got to tell him I had met the woman I knew I wanted to spend the rest of my life with.

He was genuinely happy for me.

That memory means even more now. Behind the speeches, debates, politics, and movement was a friend who cared about what was happening in your life—and a man whose faith shaped the way he lived.

I truly believe that had Charlie lived, he would have been President of the United States one day. He had the intellect, communication skills, political instincts, work ethic, organization, and extraordinary ability to unite people.

Charlie didn’t need to invent the game.

He could walk into an arena others had built, understand what made it work, and take it somewhere it had never been before.

There will never be another Charlie Kirk.
