Scripture reveals that the filling of the "cup of indignation" is not a random occurrence, but a measurable, recurring judicial principle in divine governance.

When observing the current global convergence—the open celebration of ancient high-place debauchery, the rapid consolidation of Babylon’s economic machinery, and the brazen mockery of divine moral boundaries—it mirrors the exact pressure points of past historical judgments.

Examining whether this has occurred before, and how the timing aligns with a sovereign movement of God, requires looking at the scriptural pattern of the "full cup."

1. Has This Happened Before? The Scriptural Precedents
Scripture documents several historical epochs where the cup of indignation reached capacity, triggering catastrophic divine intervention:

The Pre-Flood Generation (Genesis 6):The condition of humanity reached a state where "every intent of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually" (Genesis 6:5). The earth was filled with violence, corruption, and an absolute rejection of the Creator's boundaries. God did not strike immediately; He extended 120 years of forbearance while Noah built the ark and preached righteousness. When the cup reached the brim, judgment was total and irreversible.

The Iniquity of the Amorites (Genesis 15:16):When God made His covenant with Abraham, He explicitly told him that his descendants would dwell in Egypt for four hundred years before possessing Canaan, giving the precise judicial reason:
"For the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete [full]."God waited four centuries while the Canaanite nations established their high places, indulged in sacred prostitution, and offered their children to Molech. God did not unleash Joshua’s conquest until the spiritual cup of their abominations was completely full.

Sodom and the Cities of the Plain (Genesis 18–19):The cry against Sodom and Gomorrah became great, and their sin "very grave" (Genesis 18:20). Ezekiel 16:49–50 adds the diagnostic often overlooked: "Look, this was the iniquity of your sister Sodom: She and her daughter had pride, fullness of food, and abundance of idleness; neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy. And they were haughty and committed abomination before Me; therefore I took them away as I saw fit." The convergence of economic arrogance, neglecting the poor, and brazen sexual perversion tipped the cup.

The Destruction of the First Temple (2 Chronicles 36:14–16):Before Babylon leveled Jerusalem, the spiritual decay matched 1 Enoch 97–102:
"Moreover all the leaders of the priests and the people transgressed more and more, according to all the abominations of the nations, and defiled the house of the Lord which He had consecrated in Jerusalem. And the Lord God of their fathers sent warnings to them by His messengers... because He had compassion on His people... But they mocked the messengers of God, despised His words, and scoffed at His prophets, until the wrath of the Lord arose against His people, till there was no remedy."

In every case, delayed justice was interpreted by the wicked as divine impotence or absence—yet in every case, God was merely letting the ledger fill to the exact line of absolute justice.

2. The Mechanics of the "Cup of Indignation"

Why does God wait until the cup is full?

To Establish Indisputable Justice: When the judgment falls, no entity in heaven, earth, or under the earth can accuse God of unrighteousness or haste. The ungodly are condemned out of their own exhaustive record (as 1 Enoch 98–100 emphasizes).

To Provide Exhaustive Space for Repentance: 2 Peter 3:9 reminds us that the apparent delay is not slackness, but longsuffering, not willing that any should perish.

The Point of "No Remedy": There is a threshold where a culture or generation becomes so calcified in pride, idolatry, and suppression of truth that moral rehabilitation becomes impossible. At that exact point, judgment ceases to be merely punitive; it becomes a necessary act of cosmic sanitation.

3. Is the Timing Right for a Movement of God?

Scripturally speaking, the convergence present today strongly indicates that the timing is ripe. Throughout the biblical record, a major "movement of God" carries a dual nature: it is simultaneously a movement of crushing judgment upon the corrupt system and a movement of supernatural preservation, awakening, and vindication for the faithful remnant.

Consider the indicators aligning with Scripture:
Global Synchronization: Past judgments were regional (Canaan, Sodom, Jerusalem, Rome). The Great and Terrible Day of the Lord, as outlined in Revelation 17–18 and 1 Enoch, is the first time the high-place apparatus has become truly planetary—interconnected through instant global commerce, digital communication, and synchronized cultural apostasy.

The Arrogance of the "Privateers": Just as 1 Enoch 97 and Revelation 18 describe the merchants and elites boasting in their unassailable technological and financial security ("I sit as a queen, and am no widow, and will not see sorrow"), modern global architects openly mock accountability.

The Inversion of Truth: When Isaiah 5:20 ("Woe to those who call evil good, and good evil") moves from individual sin into enforced state and corporate policy, the societal foundations are destroyed (Psalm 11:3).

What the Truth Seeker Must Discern

When the cup is filling, people often look for a "revival" that restores the comfortable status quo, allowing them to keep their worldly alliances, their investments in Babylon, and their nominal religion.
Scripture promises something very different:

A Sifting Precedes the Shaking: Haggai 2:6–7 and Hebrews 12:26–27 declare: "Yet once more I shake not only the earth, but also heaven... that the things which cannot be shaken may remain." God does not pour out His Spirit to bless the high places; He shakes everything man has built so that only His unshakeable Kingdom stands.

The Rise of the Remnant Testimony: In 1 Enoch 100 and Malachi 3:16–18, as the darkness peaks, those who fear the Lord speak often to one another, their names written in a book of remembrance. text:
The Westminster Confession of Faith, Chapter 3, states it this way:

“God from all eternity, did, by the most wise and holy counsel of His own will, freely, and unchangeably ordain whatsoever comes to pass: yet so, as thereby neither is God the author of sin, nor is violence offered to the will of the creatures; nor is the liberty or contingency of second causes taken away, but rather established.

What this means:

Eternal and unchangeable: The decree is not a series of decisions God makes in time. It is a single, comprehensive purpose formed before creation. Nothing can alter it.

Comprehensive: It includes every event—creation, the fall, every human choice, every natural occurrence, election to salvation, and the passing over of others. Scripture is cited as saying God “works all things according to the counsel of his will” (Eph. 1:11).

Free and wise: God decrees according to His own will, not because He looked ahead and saw what creatures would do. His foreknowledge of events is the result of His decree, not its cause.

Does not make God the author of sin: God decrees that sin will occur, but He remains holy. He does NOT tempt or force anyone to sin. Human beings remain responsible for their own actions.

Does not cancel human freedom: The decree works *through* secondary causes (natural laws, human decisions, etc.) rather than bypassing them. People make real, voluntary choices; those choices simply unfold according to God’s prior plan.

A shorter catechism definition commonly used in Reformed churches is: “The decrees of God are His eternal purpose, according to the counsel of His will, whereby, for His own glory, He hath foreordained whatsoever comes to pass.”

In short, when Reformed theologians say “God decrees,” they mean that history is the outworking of an eternal, all-encompassing, wise, and holy plan that God freely formed for His own glory. Everything that happens- good and evil- falls within that plan, yet God remains righteous and human responsibility remains real.

Third, the fact that “Mystery, Babylon the Great” is also called “the mother of harlots and abominations of the earth” serves as further proof that our country is clad in the scarlet and purple robe of Revelation’s foretold and infamous spiritual whore. However, I contend that God’s judgment of America and America’s destruction, as the book Revelation predicts, came or commenced on 9/11. It has subsequently continued ever since and is soon to be completed, when “the Beast”—this fallen world’s long dreamed of New World Order—will rise from America’s ruins and lead this fallen world in its final all-out-war on God’s people, both His chosen people—Israel and the Jews—and His elect people—the church and Christians.

To prove 9/11 was God’s judgment on a God-forsaken America and that America has subsequently been being destroyed ever since, consider how we, in the immediate aftermath of 9/11, administered to ourselves a lethal injection, foolishly and fatally believing it to be an immunization from future 9/11 terrorist attacks. Right after 9/11, and for the first time in American history, our country’s citizenry voluntarily surrendered its constitutional rights and freedoms to our government in exchange for promised protection. News Flashback

Early 2026

Jan-March

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.
Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

News

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.
Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

text:
Her handwriting is all over the proof that cured tuberculosis, and her name is on none of it. Missouria Meadows-Walker wrote down every trial patient by name and fever and hour, in logbooks the doctor carried off every night in 1951.

When the cure was announced, the doctor was in every paper and she was in none.

The doctor collected the logbook from her hands every night.

In it, in her own handwriting, sat the proof. Names, fevers, every dose and every reaction, hour by hour, kept by a Black nurse named Missouria Meadows-Walker on a men's ward in Staten Island.

That logbook helped prove the cure for tuberculosis in 1952.

When the cure was announced, her name was in none of the papers.

She had come a long way to be standing at those beds. Clinton, South Carolina, the eighth of twelve children, raised by a mother everybody called Mama Amy.

Mama Amy taught her three things: to read the stars, to be fearless, and to value herself. Her family says Missouria grew into a girl who loved history and literature and jazz, and who wanted to nurse so she could, in her nephew's words, change the world and see equality for all Black people.

She went to Howard University. She studied under Estelle Massey Osborne, the first Black nurse in the country to earn a master's degree, and under the great educator Mary McLeod Bethune.

After she graduated, she worked closely with Dr. Charles Drew, whose research on storing blood plasma was already saving lives that would never know his name either.

Then she folded her white uniform into a suitcase, got on a train heading north, and went to work at a hospital most of New York was afraid to enter.

Sea View sat on a hilltop on Staten Island, four hundred feet up, three hundred acres, eight tall pavilions full of people dying of tuberculosis.

They called it the Pest House. It was where the city sent its poorest consumptives, the ones no one else would touch.

In the spring of 1929, the white nurses had started walking out. The disease was taking them too, the commute was long, and they were finished.

So the city went looking for nurses who had no better choice.

At the time, only four of New York's twenty-nine municipal hospitals would hire a Black nurse at all. A Black woman with a nursing degree was shut out of nearly every hospital in America, North and South.

Sea View would take her. It offered steady pay, housing, and a job in an integrated hospital, far from the back doors and the colored fountains and the daily insults of the Jim Crow South.

The catch was the disease itself. Untreated active tuberculosis killed roughly four out of five people who carried it, and there was no cure, only bed rest and surgery.

To keep a ruined lung from collapsing, surgeons would deflate it on purpose and prop the cavity with small objects, even ping-pong balls. The nurses stood at the bedside for all of it, breathing the same air, every shift, for decades.

So the best job a Black nurse in America could get was also one of the most dangerous in the city. Missouria took it.

They put her on the men's ward.

A man who worked under her years later tried to describe that ward to the writer Maria Smilios. Think of it like a rough bar at night, he told her, where the men snuck out, came back drunk, and the fistfights never really stopped.

On that ward, Missouria absorbed a barrage of racial abuse, shift after shift, from patients who hated her and said so to her face.

Then, in 1944, a new patient was wheeled in. He was a Nazi prisoner of war, gravely sick with TB, and because of the disease he had been sent to Sea View and placed on Missouria's ward, under her care.

He despised her on sight. Day after day he told her the same thing, that he hoped she would catch what he had and not survive it.

She nursed him anyway. For about a year, Missouria Meadows-Walker kept alive a man who openly wished her dead.

Her niece would later try to explain how a person does that. "This was her calling," the niece said, "and she stayed the course and believed God would help work it out."

By the mid-1940s, after years on that ward, she was promoted to supervisor.

That promotion was not small. At Sea View, supervisor jobs were almost always reserved for white nurses, and here was a Black woman from South Carolina running the floor.

Her great-niece, Florence Shirley, once put Missouria's whole character into a single sentence. "Her calling was to take care of the patients," Shirley said, "and she didn't care what disease they had as long as she was able to take care of them and get them healthy."

She knew her patients by name, by mood, by history. Soon that knowledge would matter more than anyone in a laboratory could have guessed.

In May of 1951, a drug company quietly brought Sea View's acting medical director, Dr. Edward Robitzek, a compound that had cured tuberculosis in mice and guinea pigs and had never once been given to a human being.

It was called isoniazid. No one knew the side effects, and no one knew whether it would heal a person or hurt them.

The whole thing started in secret. When word later reached the National Tuberculosis Association that Sea View was involved, they actually told Robitzek to keep the findings quiet.

Robitzek chose five patients so far gone that nothing else had worked, and asked if they were willing to try. Then he chose the people who would actually run the trial at the bedside.

He picked Missouria Meadows-Walker. He picked Edna Sutton, Janie Shirley, Clemmie Phillips, and Stiversa Bethel.

He picked them because they had spent decades on those wards and understood the disease the way only someone holding a dying man's wrist can understand it. He needed nurses who would catch the smallest shift in a patient before it became the difference between a breakthrough and a tragedy.

In June 1951, the nurses gave the trial patients the first dose. Then they did not look away.

Three times a day they administered the medication. They took vitals, watched whether a man could suddenly breathe easier, whether a fever finally broke, whether appetite came creeping back, whether something new and frightening was beginning instead.

Every observation went into the logbooks in their own handwriting. Every single evening, Robitzek carried those books away and read what the nurses had seen.

And what the nurses were seeing was almost impossible to believe. Men who had been sent to Sea View to die were sitting up in bed. Eating. Asking to be let outside.

On February 20, 1952, the news broke wide open. The New York Post splashed it across the front page: "Wonder Drug Fights TB."

Photographers rushed to Sea View and found patients who, only months before, had been left for dead, now up on their feet and dancing in the halls. Those photographs ran in papers across the entire country.

It was one of the biggest medical stories of the century. It was real, it changed the world, and these nurses had helped make it real.

Dr. Robitzek's name was everywhere in the coverage. He was quoted, credited, and remembered.

Missouria's name was in none of it. Neither was Edna's, or Janie's, or Clemmie's, or Stiversa's.

The women whose handwriting filled the very logbooks that proved the drug worked were left out of the story of the drug entirely.

Three years later, in 1955, the achievement won the Albert Lasker Award, one of the highest honors in American medicine. It went to Robitzek and three other doctors.

Not one nurse was named.

So the nurses went back to work. They had children to raise, mortgages to carry on houses the city had tried to redline them out of, an entire Black middle-class community to build on Staten Island that still stands today.

And the books they had filled, page after page, in their own steady hands, sat in the historical record under other people's names.

Here is the part the headlines left out.

Robitzek himself knew exactly what those women had done. Late in his life he said it plainly, that none of it would have been possible without the nurses.

He said it out loud. It just never made the front page.

For seventy years, that was where the whole thing stayed.

Then a writer named Maria Smilios, editing a medical book about rare lung diseases, stopped cold on a single sentence that mentioned a cure found at Sea View. She went looking for the women behind it.

She found almost nothing at all. "These women had been completely erased from history," Smilios said. "There was not a single thing about them."

There were no archives of their work, no official record of their names on the trial that changed medicine. So she rebuilt it from the ground up.

It took her roughly eight years. She did it almost entirely from oral history, from families pulling out old photographs and letters, from women remembering aloud at kitchen tables what their aunts and mothers had once carried.

Missouria's own family carried her back into the light, the same way Mama Amy had once taught a little girl in South Carolina to find her way home by the stars.

Her story sits in a book now, "The Black Angels," with Missouria Louvinia Meadows-Walker's name printed inside it for anyone to read.

Her photograph hangs on the wall of the Staten Island Museum, a young Black woman in a crisp white uniform, looking back at every person who comes to stand in front of her.

And her name is in the Congressional Record of the United States, entered so the Black Angels of Sea View can never be quietly dropped from the story again.

Missouria spent her working life writing other people's names into the record so the truth of what happened to them would outlast them. Hour by hour, fever by fever, in her own hand.

It only took seventy years for someone to do the same for her.

I put a lot of effort into researching and sharing stories that matter.
If you'd like to support the work, here's the link:
https://t.co/AeER0VXKqi
Every coffee helps me keep creating.

text:
He bought the exact Chieftain he crewed at seventeen.
I keep coming back to the four crew positions behind this reunion: commander, gunner, loader and driver (four men, each depending on the other three).
The man beside “Bobby Dee” is former British Army gunner Rob Dove. This is not merely the same kind of tank. Registration 05EB53 proves it is the Chieftain he crewed with the 15th/19th The King’s Royal Hussars.
Based in Detmold, West Germany, Dove and his crew trained aboard it for two years. Their 56-tonne Chieftain carried call sign 20 and a 120mm gun. They had to be ready if Soviet armour ever crossed into the West.
That battle never came.
Decades later, Dove discovered 05EB53 was for sale. His first offer was refused. Once its owners understood that he had served inside this very tank, a deal was struck.
He bought it in 2023 and spent two years bringing it back, even restoring the markings it carried during his service. At Eden Camp, he climbed inside his old crew station again.
Its survival preserves more than British engineering. It keeps the crew’s working world intact—and remembers the soldiers who prepared for a war everyone hoped would never begin.

#OTTAWA
 — A former senior Canadian defence official suing the federal government over a dismissal her lawyer links to (Mark Carney’s) pivot toward #China is pointing to the government’s newly disclosed military engagement with #Beijing 
— and to what she calls growing public recognition that Canada’s partnership with China has impeded trade talks with #Washington.

"Raquel Garbers" was the principal architect of the small team that drafted Canada’s 2024 defence policy, Our North, Strong and Free. On Oct. 15, 2025, she published an opinion piece warning that Ottawa’s increasingly anti-American rhetoric was dividing the Western alliance and benefiting Beijing and #Moscow.

Those hostile states — principally China — had been waging a covert war against Canada and the United States for about a decade, Garbers wrote. Two days later, Foreign Affairs Minister "Anita Anand" was in Beijing describing China as a strategic partner. Four weeks after that, Garbers was told her position was being eliminated.

She filed a wrongful-dismissal claim in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice in June. In an interview, Garbers’ lawyer said Carney’s strategic pivot toward Beijing had chilled parts of Ottawa’s bureaucracy and created a perception that Garbers was fired as a warning to others. None of the allegations has been tested in court.

Writing on LinkedIn on Monday, Garbers responded to a story The Bureau published the same day: Canada’s military had formally reopened its Defence Coordination Dialogue with the People’s Liberation Army on Sept. 4, but Canadians learned of the meeting only through a two-paragraph notice from China’s defence ministry.

“The [government] mismanaged the public politics of its defence/military deal with Beijing,” Garbers wrote. “In staying silent while Beijing shouted about it across the globe, Ottawa handed Beijing a major propaganda win.”

Garbers’ second point concerned Carney’s collapsed trade talks with the Trump administration.

Days before the Victoria military conference opened — an event attended by a Chinese delegation led by General Yang Zhibin, commander of the PLA’s Eastern Theater Command — Carney was describing Canada’s relationship with Washington in warlike terms.

“Last evening, I instructed our negotiators to return to Ottawa,” he said on Aug. 22. “We cannot accept what they’ve offered, and we will not give what they’ve asked.”

That same day, he characterized the relationship this way: “You’re at war when you get attacked. We got attacked.”

In her LinkedIn post, Garbers argued that Ottawa’s failure to disclose the renewed engagement with the People’s Liberation Army means media “coverage of the deal will put Ottawa’s reputation for accommodating China front of mind just as the public is realizing that its partnership with Beijing played a pivotal role in crashing CUSMA talks.”

Garbers’ third point was sharper, presenting the implications of Canadian military cooperation with Beijing as an unavoidable factor in relations between Ottawa and Washington.

“[With respect to] questions [around] the impact on US relations, the [government] must either admit de facto US ‘consent’ of the deal (a blow to its domestic chops) or it must deny US ‘consent’ (a win for DC’s claim that [Canada] is Beijing’s backdoor into the US).”

Put plainly, Garbers argues that Ottawa faces two politically damaging possibilities.

If it says Washington knew about the military engagement and did not object, Ottawa risks appearing to concede that a sovereign Canadian defence decision required the approval of the administration Carney has described as attacking Canada. If it says Washington was unaware, it lends support to an argument already circulating in the U.S. capital: that Canada offers Beijing a back door into American security.

text:
I grew up next to the Twin Towers. The little town of Union Beach, New Jersey, sits on the Raritan Bay. On a clear day, you can see across the water to the New York City skyline.

On September 11, 2001, there was not a cloud in the sky as I boarded a school bus to my high school, the Marine Academy of Science and Technology (@MAST_SandyHook). Located at the end of Sandy Hook, M.A.S.T. is even closer to lower Manhattan than Union Beach.

When tragedy struck, my classmates and I were so close that phone lines jammed and the sky turned black with smoke. For days, we could see and smell the smoke from Ground Zero.

I volunteered to serve in the United States Army because of September 11, 2001. Still, the words I offer feel hollow when compared to the magnitude of the tragedy.

Twenty-five years later, I struggle to think about it. We lost 2,977 blessed souls. The pain felt by their families is unimaginable.

I look to survivor Michael Hingson, who said, “I may never know the answers to the questions that plagued me after 9/11. But I know if we lean on God and each other we will be guided to a better, brighter future.”

Today, I remember those we lost, those who survived, those who came to their rescue, and the loved ones who remain. Lest we forget.

**"I want drivers, cooks, the woman selling food in the streets to invest." Powerful words from Aliko Dangote. Here's the fundamentals-first read on the moment.**

The story making headlines today: African leaders — Dangote himself, Amb. Jendayi Frazer, Governor Sanwo-Olu — rallying behind the Dangote Refinery IPO as a chance for "ordinary Africans" to own a piece of the continent's biggest industrial asset. Dangote drew comparisons to Amazon, Tesla, Microsoft — companies that scaled after going public.

**It's genuinely inspiring. It's also not a valuation.**

Here's the distinction every investor needs to hold in their head at the same time:

✅ The MISSION is legitimate — broadening ownership beyond a handful of billionaires and pension funds is a real, positive shift for African capital markets.

✅ The BUSINESS is real — audited numbers, a functioning refinery, genuine operational turnaround.

⚠️ But neither of those things changes what we already know about the PRICE: ~18x EV/EBITDA against global refining peers trading at 8.5-10.5x, with the bulls' own downside case sitting below the ₦525 offer.

**Inspiring rhetoric and sound investing aren't opposites — but they're not the same thing either.** A teacher in Enugu deserves the chance to own a piece of African industry. She also deserves to know exactly what she's paying for it, not just why it matters.

Believe in the vision. Verify the numbers. Do both — that's not cynicism, that's respect for your own money.

Fundamentals first. Always. We look before we leap.

text:
9/11: The nightmares returned this year after a long period of calm. A friend and former colleague, John Howell, helped make the memorial below in Charlotte happen. The FF Steven Coakley Foundation put it together. 

We met years later and discovered he was across the street as I was in the Marriott World Trade Center. I still carry my key card with me everywhere I go as a talisman.

He lost his brother, a fire fighter doing what he did best. I bear the scars of the toxins in the air and the cancers that took even more of us in the years that followed. Mine arrived in the middle of the pandemic. 

I believe that we carry the spirits of those we love most in this world through our actions, which amplifies their memory and keeps their spirits alive. Their lives are like the ripple of a pebble after it hits the surface of a pond. 

It is hard to explain how one event can mark one’s life. It is harder to grapple with how that same event hurt those you love most. 

Terrorism is not new but a constant; it has taken too many souls from this world and continues as a shadow, long after the dust seeps into every aspect of your being.

I was but a visitor in NY that day. The burden of my choice of the location has never quite lifted. Lightening can strike twice. My task is to weather the storm, rebuild, move forward, one step at a time.

Then memories I hold onto most were the acts kindness and humanity amidst the chaos. My colleague who took the names and numbers of survivors to let their loved ones know they were alive. The bus driver who let us on to help in our trek up the FDR. The restaurant owner that gave us water and a moment of rest amidst the chaos. The doorman who called my name as I reached Central Park late in the day. My name tag was still attached to my lapel. The music of children’s laughter playing in the park still dances in my ears. I was lost, trying to find my to a friend and journalist who offered to take me in. 

He took my hand, covered in the soot of all that was lost that day, guided me to the corner and handed me off to strangers. Each one, extended a hand where the last left off. Each touch was a reminder of our collective humanity, a hope that still sustains me. 

That is why I end each monthly piece I write these days with: Be kind; pay it forward. 

I know how much random acts of kindness can save a life and redeem a soul. I ❤️NY.

Whiskey Jug Genie by Sultonna Nadine is a lighthearted and charming paranormal fantasy that mixes magic, humor, and a touch of romance for pure escapist fun.

When quiet London apothecary shop owner Martin buys an old whiskey jug on vacation, he has no idea he’s about to release Bubba, a genie who’s been trapped inside for 200 years and is thoroughly out of touch with the modern world. Chaos, spells, cultural clashes, and plenty of laughs ensue as the unlikely pair (along with a very annoyed cat) try to navigate the mess. Set against the backdrop of contemporary London with elements of white magic and everyday wonder, the story balances humorous situations with warmer moments. Readers appreciate its playful tone, quirky characters, and the perfect blend of paranormal fantasy, magic, and comedy—it’s the kind of book that delivers smiles and a welcome dose of whimsy.

text:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari offered prayers at Kolkata’s Kalighat Temple on the occasion of Kaushiki Amavasya and ate traditional fish bhog offered to Maa Kali.

Adhikari visited the temple on Thursday, where he participated in special prayers and offered a Banarasi saree and flowers to the deity. After the rituals, he sat on the floor inside the temple premises and ate basanti pulao, fried fish and fish head served as bhog.

His visit came amid a growing debate in West Bengal over non vegetarian food during religious festivals.

Adhikari Defends Bengali Food Traditions

Speaking to reporters, Adhikari said Kaushiki Amavasya was an important occasion in Sanatan culture. He said special prayers were being held at major temples, including Kalighat in Kolkata and Tarapith in Birbhum district.

On the controversy over non vegetarian food, Adhikari said religious practices could coexist with Bengali food traditions.

text:
She never married, yet she still considers herself Captain Vikram Batra's widow.

Inside every girl, there is a lover waiting to drown in love. 
The Quint ran a beautiful story on Captain Vikram Batra back in 2016. 
That hero was someone's absolute everything. 
The way his girlfriend described their four-year relationship—imagining how she must still feel, even 17 years later, brought me to tears.

In 1995, both enrolled in the M.A. English program at Panjab University, though neither completed the postgraduate degree. 
Dimple Cheema, Vikram's girlfriend, says that perhaps destiny brought them to that university just so they could meet. 
She still remembers how happily and excitedly Vikram shared the news of his selection into the Indian Military Academy (IMA). 
That moment sealed their relationship—a rare feat, considering how many relationships crumble under the pressure of career uncertainty.

Once Vikram left for his training, they barely had time together. 
Back home, talk of Dimple's marriage began. 
When she mentioned this to Vikram, he offered a piece of quiet wisdom: "Take care of what you like, or you will be forced to like whatever you get."

They often visited the Mansa Devi Temple and Gurudwara Sri Nada Sahib together. 
During one visit to the temple, while circumambulating the shrine for the fourth time, Vikram turned, held the edge of her dupatta, and whispered, "Congratulations, Mrs. Batra!" 
On another occasion, under intense family pressure to marry and feeling deeply insecure about their future, Dimple snapped at him. 
Vikram calmly pulled a blade from his wallet, cut his thumb, and filled the parting of her hair with his blood. 
For a long time after, Dimple teasingly called him "totally filmy."

Today, decades later, those moments are the memories she lives by. 
It was settled that they would marry as soon as Vikram returned from Kargil. 
Instead, he returned wrapped in the tricolor. 
Every time I ponder this, my heart breaks and I feel like sobbing uncontrollably. 
What must go through the heart of a lover left with nothing but unfulfilled promises and sacred memories?

Recalling Vikram, Dimple describes him as a perpetually restless soul. 
At restaurants, he would tap his car keys against the table until the food arrived. 
If she stopped him, he would put the keys down and tap his fingers. 
If she scolded him for that, he would start fidgeting his legs. 
And if she glared at him to make him stop, having nothing left to do, he would gulp down water—drinking like someone who had been thirsty for years.

To think that a woman can smile and keep living, holding onto such tiny, intricate details years later, is both bone-chilling and deeply moving. 
Dimple never saw him on the battlefield, but knowing him as intimately as she did, she could visualize his exact reactions. 
She lived through his every breath. 
We construct a person out of these small nuances, understanding them better than they know themselves, losing ourselves entirely in them. What a transcendent experience that must be.

She continues to cherish his memory after all this time. 
In our society, when a girl falls in love, parents often remain indifferent. 
They marry her off to whomever they choose, clinging to the flawed logic that "time heals all wounds and she will eventually forget."

Listening to a tale of such profound love makes one want to surrender to it entirely, yet such love is not granted to everyone. 
People often label casual relationships as love, but few ever dive into its true depth. 
As painful as Dimple's story is to read, I also consider her remarkably blessed. 
Every girl deserves a lover who cherishes her deeply and understands her—someone who prioritizes her over material wealth. 
Every girl deserves a lover upon whom she can bestow her devotion without hesitation, on whose shoulder she can rest her head and forget the chaos of the world.

text: Today's news has disappointed his students. Those who once prayed before his sacred objects, visited his vihara, or placed their faith in him may begin to wonder, "What is truly the value of everything I've believed in all this time?" More regrettably, this situation is also a painful reminder that robes cannot conceal greed, titles cannot sanctify hypocrisy, and sacred objects cannot replace genuine virtue. When the very person entrusted with teaching detachment and purity is revealed to have hoarded wealth and broken the most basic precepts, the damage goes far beyond one temple. It quietly erodes the trust of countless ordinary devotees who offered their money, time, and sincere faith, believing they were supporting the Dhamma rather than a man's private life. True refuge was never meant to rest in any individual, no matter how revered. It rests only in the teaching itself.

text:
GROK BOT HOW TO USE
Sources: official https://t.co/2EN1BbJ794 + https://t.co/0OVb26msAp + your Grok Bot bookmark folder (866 posts)
Updated: 2026-09-11

WHAT NEW TODAY
- Folder 866 posts (7 new vs Sep 10)
- Testers (unicodef1wn): 10 official-docs rules before upgrading for weekly limits — meters steps/tokens not messages; scope tight; check Weekly usage; connector first; save skills; test before schedule; never every-new-message; audit routines; keep work in /workspace; plans don’t stack
- Testers (XFreeze): sales connectors — Salesforce, HubSpot, Gong, Clay, Granola + GTM; SpaceXAI sales-team Bot templates
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker): redesigned Marketplace; chat right pane Media/Computer/Routines; Voice calls coming (not live yet)
- Testers (techdevnotes): Desktop Network Debugger
- Official Elon (quoting bot): amplify draft-before-send QoL
- Testers (aaronburnett): Bret called Grok Bot a “viral product” on consumer side; enterprise slower

WHAT IT IS
- A Bot is a named, persistent teammate, not a one-off chat
- You message it like a coworker and it finishes work in real apps
- All of your Bots share one cloud computer (browser, files, terminal)
- Each Bot has its own screen on that shared computer
- Work keeps going when your laptop or the app is closed
- It only comes back when it needs approval or a human step
- Do not confuse Grok Bot with Digital Optimus (real-time video human emulation)
- Testers (joehansen): do not confuse Grok Bot with an X Chat Agent (an X account you add to a group chat). Grok Bot is the machine that does the work
- Official Elon: Your Bot will identify issues to resolve, notify you when they are fixed, and continue on with your project

ACCESS AND INSTALL
- Official bot (Aug 26): All SuperGrok and Cursor Pro subscribers now have access
- Testers (mattyp): Grok Bot is free to try; every Grok & Cursor plan includes Grok Bot
- Testers quoting SpaceXAI (cb_doge): SuperGrok, SuperGrok Plus, SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor Pro, Cursor Pro+, Cursor Ultra, Cursor Teams Standard and Premium
- Cursor CEO Michael Truell: everyone with a standard Grok or Cursor subscription
- Testers: included at no extra cost with those plans; circulating plan prices $20/month Cursor Pro and $25/month SuperGrok (nextbigfuture)
- Official bot + Elon: weekly / free usage limits reset for all Grok Bot users
- Sign in with your Cursor account (that account owns plan and usage)
Official desktop download: https://t.co/C9n6VM80SO
- Also listed at https://t.co/jeYLjt4xIM
- Official desktop is macOS and Windows (Apple silicon or Intel; Windows x64 or Arm64)
- Testers (mattyp): Linux is now supported (official docs may lag)
- iPhone: iOS 18+, App Store app "Grok Bot"
- Official (bot, Sep 2): Grok Bot is now available on Android
- Testers (mark_k): install from Play Store; full Grok Bot experience on Android
- Play Store: https://t.co/CM2CGVPiuU
- Official docs may still lag on Android; Testers (mattyp, Sep 4): Grok Bot is now available for iPad
- SuperGrok Heavy users can choose Get access with SuperGrok Heavy, then Link Grok Account
- Linking SuperGrok Heavy can unlock free Cursor Ultra (one Grok account to one Cursor account)
- Testers (unicodef1wn, Sep 10): plans don’t stack — linking SuperGrok to a Cursor plan adds zero usage; upgrade within Cursor or turn on on-demand if you need more
- Legacy Privacy Mode blocks Grok Bot; switch to a supported Cursor data setting first
- Grok Bot checks for updates automatically; Check for Updates is in Settings → Beta
- Official Elon (Sep 4): Grok Bot Enterprise is now available
- Testers (mark_k, Sep 3): Version 0.36.0 is now live — bugfixes and improvements
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Sep 9): Version 0.47.0 — auto lock team review; auto review team rules
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Sep 9): Version 0.44.0 — marketplace of bots; multi-person Bot; voice overheard/speech tags
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Sep 10): Marketplace redesign + chat right pane + Voice calls coming (not live yet)
- Testers (techdevnotes, Sep 9): Desktop Network Debugger
- Testers (mattyp, Sep 4): iPad app available (official docs may still lag)

SIGN IN
[] Desktop: Get started, then Sign In with Cursor in the browser
[] iOS: Login with Cursor, finish in the browser, return to the app
[] Official: Cmd-D turns on voice dictation
[] Official: it is easier to use the remote computer from your phone
[] Use the same Cursor account that should own usage
[] First-run tour asks which tools you use; that only shapes teammate suggestions
[] Computer setup runs in the background, then Meet a future teammate opens

CREATE A BOT
[] New in the sidebar, or Cmd/Ctrl+N
[] In New chat, choose Create new agent
[] Edit Profile: name, title, description, avatar
[] Give a short name, one primary job, and how it should work
[] Description = standing rules (never send without approval)
[] Chat messages = this-task instructions (draft follow-ups for these 12 accounts)
[] Focused Bots beat one catch-all General Helper
[] Testers (XFreeze): do not design a Bot from scratch; ask a Bot to create a capable one for you (it already has your context)
[] Bookmark testers: start with about six roles; give each Bot recurring work
[] Pin important Bots; hide unused ones (hiding does not pause routines)
[] Bookmark testers: resize the sidebar, give titles, and group Bots into sections
[] Duplicate a Bot to reuse a role for a new scope (copy does not include memory or history)
[] Delete only if you are sure; files and logins on the shared computer stay
[] Account limit: 50 Bots and group chats combined
[] Name language can steer reply language (bookmark testers reported this)
[] Bookmark testers: no model picker yet; testers still list BYOK, multiplayer, and hang-error messages as missing (iPad now available per mattyp); SpaceXAI notes voice calls coming with voice/speed/language picks (not live yet per blankspeaker)

[] Testers (XEthanai / XFreeze): shareable Bot templates - build once, fine-tune, share the full setup for others to use or customize
[] Testers (GrokBotDev): Official Marketplace launched (about 69 bots listed; community has catalogued 420+ searchable from a Bot)
[] SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker): v0.44.0 worked on browse a marketplace of bots; use a Bot with more than one person; overheard/speech tags on voice
[] SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Sep 10): redesigned Marketplace coming — plugins and bots on the front page, For You, Featured, categories, search, and installed (not live yet)
[] Testers (XFreeze, Sep 10): SpaceXAI releasing actual sales-team Bots as installable templates (prebuilt context, connectors, routines)
[] Testers (XFreeze): Marketplace framing earlier — browse specialized Grok Bots by category and add them to your team
[] Testers (RoundtableSpace): Marketplace framing — hand-picked bots by category with routines/workflows built in (app store for AI teammates)
[] Testers (kloss_xyz): 8 official-ish bot templates (calls, X, writing, images, coding, networking, tool testing, parking tickets)
HOW TO WRITE A TASK
[] Outcome: what should be finished
[] Testers (unicodef1wn): Grok Bot meters agent steps and tokens, not messages — vague tasks wander and burn the week; scope with Task / Work in / Context / Done means / first N items then stop
[] Sources: which apps, sites, files, or chats matter
[] Constraints: what it must not do, or must ask first
[] Deliverable: what it should return
[] Review point: when it should stop for you
[] Safe first task: attach a file and ask for a cited summary; do not change the file
[] Next task: one real tool, read-only, with a sign-in handoff if needed
[] After a good result, name the lasting format preference in chat
[] Then save it as a skill or routine
[] Official bot examples: email cleanup, Starlink-likely flights, build a site then buy the domain and deploy, meeting notes, sales prospecting, refunds, podcast audio digest
[] Testers: paste a viral video link and ask the Bot to recreate it
[] Testers: start from an org chart or make one Bot the boss of a repo, not a long to-do list
[] Testers: one clear job, explicit allowed sources, no-guessing rule, approval gate before any real action
[] Testers: 5 calibrations - confidence threshold, checkpoint long tasks, show negative examples, gate destructive actions separately, test edge cases first
[] Testers: one Bot, one job - two jobs claimed worse at both; put recurring work on a schedule
[] Testers quoting claimed SpaceXAI employee: version prompts and tool configs like code; scratchpad separate from the user-facing answer; retry with a different strategy; measure cost per successful outcome; review failure logs on a schedule
[] Testers (mvanhorn): Compound Engineering - force a plan first; three-layer instructions (base, role, current focus); screenshot instead of retyping what's on screen; ping only on a real hit
[] Testers (AlexFinn): anything you are about to do on your computer, ask Grok Bot first
[] Testers (AlexFinn): example week - Reddit microSaaS, 3D digital office to watch Bots, Omarchy setup, product returns, daily AI news post, Cursor cloud-agent bug fixes, X model-release watch, brand-deal negotiation, contract redlines
[] Testers (Michael_Fenech_): give it business responsibilities (checking, chasing, updating, coordinating), not just questions

AGENT COMPUTER AND LOGINS
[] Open Agent Computer from the conversation to watch the desktop
[] Testers (techdevnotes, Sep 9): Grok Bot Desktop now has Network Debugger
[] SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Sep 10): chat right pane coming — Media, Computer (watch the bot’s screen), and Routines (not live yet)
[] Take over for password, passkey, 2FA, CAPTCHA, payment, or human-only pages
[] Complete only the blocked step, then return control
[] Never paste passwords or one-time codes into chat
[] Official (bot, Sep 8): fill out forms and logins for your Bot without ever leaving the chat, with support for any password manager
[] Testers (XFreeze): when a site needs your account, Bot pauses; you auth with 1Password / Apple Passwords / any manager; Bot continues — no pasting credentials into chat
[] Testers (LaceyPresley / muskonomy): in-chat logins/forms also cover checkouts and booking flights
[] Grok Bot team (poteto, Sep 9): account switching is finally here
[] Official (bot, Sep 9): Share a file directly with Grok Bot on mobile
[] Use a secure secret request when the app offers one
[] Browser sessions persist and are shared across all your Bots
[] Prefer a connector/plugin when one exists; use the browser when it does not
[] Coinbase (coinbase, Sep 9): Coinbase for Agents on Grok — connect Coinbase at https://t.co/aL6KKYjGXH; tell Grok to trade, analyze, automate; no MCP setup
[] Testers (XFreeze, Sep 10): sales/GTM connectors — Salesforce, HubSpot, Gong, Clay, Granola + other GTM tools so Bots can pull account context, research prospects, prepare follow-ups
[] Testers (SamSokolin): for repeated web-app clicks, reverse-engineer browser-use into scripts (capture network once, call APIs next)
[] Keep durable files in /workspace with clear project folders
[] Settings → Beta: Update Agent Computer (preserve state), Recover, or Reset (can lose recent work)
[] The cloud computer is not your Mac or Windows machine
[] Local-computer execution is separate: Settings → General → Agent → Execution on Local Computer
[] Default local policy is Ask every time; use Never allowed unless you need local files
[] Bookmark testers: give a Bot full local Mac/iMessage access only on a spare machine
[] Testers: local Mac access can write local Python scripts on your Mac
[] Testers (Av1dlive / mvanhorn): Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor claimed runnable on the Bot's own computer
[] Testers (XFreeze): take over that same cloud computer from your phone without being at the laptop
[] Testers (Damir_Akaza): group-chat Bots can reach a local Mac Mini via Tailscale for project files and local scripts
[] Testers (farzyness): a Bot can exclusively use Grok Build in CLI with the latest Grok models at highest thinking
[] Testers (AlexFinn): a 3D digital office on a second monitor to watch Bots work

PLUGINS AND CONNECTORS
[] Settings → Plugins, then Add, then authenticate in the browser
[] Grok Bot team (poteto): tinkabot helps build MCP/skills plugins and submit them for approval so all users can use them
[] Type @ to attach a connector; type / to reference a saved skill
[] Installed connectors are account-wide, not isolated to one Bot
[] Official: you can connect multiple accounts to the same plugin
[] Official bot (Aug 26): SuperGrok and Cursor Pro now included; weekly limits reset. Testers quoting SpaceXAI: also Plus/Heavy/Pro+/Ultra/Teams
[] Testers: give a Bot its own email address so it can send and receive on its own
[] Testers (mvanhorn): give a Bot its own inbox, not your Gmail (one mistake should not flag your domain); Twilio number so a Bot can make calls
[] Testers: app v0.23.0 adds creating new channels
[] Official bot: improved X support - connect your X profile; a developer account is auto-created with included credits
[] Testers (blankspeaker): Plugins, add X, authenticate; $100 in X API credits good for a year (new and existing devs)
[] Testers (GrokInsider): if credits did not land, ask Grok Bot to connect X so the Authorize card opens the browser; tester's manual plugin add failed
[] Follow the Connect card when a Bot asks for a plugin
[] Bookmark testers: X connector may still need a paid X API key in some setups (official path now auto-creates a developer account with credits)
[] Bookmark testers: image generation works; testers now also claim video editing (music sync). Video generation still unconfirmed. Testers (XFreeze): dedicated video-editor Bot for footage → clips/cuts/sound/titles
[] Bookmark testers: Grok Bot can now read your X bookmarks
[] Testers (testerlabor): you can link your X Premium+ subscription to Grok Bot
[] Testers: Higgsfield x Grok Bot; 100 free credits for new users
[] Testers: send a YouTube link with start/end timestamps and get an HD clip in chat (Google login claimed)
[] Testers: give a Bot Grok Build + Cursor CLI so weekly limits can be spread across Cursor and Grok

[] Grok Bot team (poteto) + testers (XFreeze): Microsoft connectors live - Outlook, Outlook Calendar, OneDrive (search/send email, drafts, schedules, meetings, browse/upload files)
[] Testers (XFreeze): Bot can natively generate images with Grok Imagine Image 2.0 inside the workflow (no separate Imagine tab)
SKILLS AND ROUTINES
[] Skill = reusable how-to (steps, rules, output, approval boundary)
[] Routine = when to run that work (schedule or event)
[] Do the task once, make it reliable, save a skill, then automate
[] Teach a task: open computer view, choose Teach a task, demo up to 10 minutes, review the draft skill
[] Teaching records the screen, not microphone audio; do not expose secrets while teaching
[] If Teach a task is missing, ask the Bot to write a skill from the completed work
[] Create a routine on the Bot that should own the job
[] Confirm owner, schedule, time zone, input, result, approval, and missing-data behavior
[] Event triggers (Slack, GitHub) are separate from plugins and need their own connection
[] Keep event matchers narrow; avoid every new message
[] Testers (unicodef1wn): never trigger on every new message (docs warn broad listeners eat usage); pick one channel and one keyword; audit forgotten dailies
[] Testers (unicodef1wn): add to every routine — if the source is unavailable, report the failure instead of using old data; test run before you schedule
[] Test run does real work; use safe inputs
[] Testers quoting docs: Test can send real emails to real clients; Stop is a brake, not a rewind
[] View conversation details → Routines to pause, edit, inspect, or delete
[] A Bot can own 50 routines; last 20 run records are kept
[] Deleting a routine has no undo
[] Testers quoting docs: delete a Bot and every routine on it dies; no undo
[] Long absence can pause unattended routines until you confirm
[] Bookmark testers: Teach a task from + in the browser, record yourself, then let the Bot replay it
[] Testers: skills taught to one bot claimed available across the account team on the same computer
[] Official Elon: how to share your Grok Bot design with others
[] Testers: a reusable-skills source claimed (BrianRoemmele)
[] Testers quoting Grok Bot team (0xMorlex): keep recurring routines off the main agent's context
[] Testers (mvanhorn): Teach by recording and respect the 10-minute cap

MULTI BOT TEAMS
[] Start with one Bot that owns an end-to-end outcome
[] Add a specialist only when the role is stable
[] Use a group chat when the handoff itself should be visible
[] SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker): v0.44.0 worked on using a Grok Bot with more than one person
[] Bots can message each other and pass ownership
[] Do not treat separate Bots as a security boundary (they share the computer)
[] Keep sending, buying, deleting, publishing, and production changes behind approval
[] Bookmark testers: a Bot may create other Bots before it can delete them
[] Bookmark testers: tell a hub Bot to loop a specialist every few minutes and watch it
[] Testers: put Bots in one group chat, appoint a Chief of Staff, and stop being the router
[] Testers (farzyness): one master agent owns specialists + chat rooms and pings you one action item at a time
[] Testers: isolate each Bot's job and add a supervisor; a crew without that can perform worse
[] Testers: night-shift crews (chief, scout, forge, critic, ship, ledger) share one computer; human gate for merge, production, spend, send, delete
[] Testers: one group chat per job/post, not per Bot; you only message the Chief of Staff
[] Testers: show the workflow once on screen rather than writing a long spec
[] Testers: add a RED TEAM Bot whose job is to disprove the thesis; no single source closes a claim
[] Testers quoting Grok Bot team (0xMorlex): specialist roles (designer/engineer/PM); organize projects without a new Bot for everything; a Chief of Agents that creates and manages the rest
[] Testers (mvanhorn): Bot Advisor whose only job is building and tightening other Bots; files are the memory bus between Bots
[] Testers (Damir_Akaza): 4 Bots in one group chat split a Meta ads campaign (creatives, fact-check, deploy) with autonomous handoff

[] Testers (cminshall): overnight group of five Bots one-shotted an admin UI from PRD/FRD/prototype PNGs
IOS
[] Same Bots, chats, routines, plugins, and cloud computer as desktop
[] Testers (mattyp): Grok Bot supports 21+ localized languages on mobile
[] Send text, dictate, attach photos/files, mention Bots, reply in threads
[] Take over the computer for login/2FA from the phone
[] You can pause or resume a routine on iOS
[] Editing schedule, run history, test, delete, and teach-by-demo still need desktop
[] Enable notifications for results, questions, and approvals
[] Testers: phone notification shows the proposed action; approve or deny
[] Testers (XFreeze): you can operate and take over the Bot's computer from your phone as long as it has internet
[] Grok Bot team (poteto, earlier): had pointed at Play pre-registration; superseded by Official bot Sep 2 Android launch

APPROVALS AND SAFETY
[] Put the stop line in the request: draft, do not send; ask after showing current vs proposed
[] Official (bot, Sep 9): ask your Bot to draft messages inline for you to approve before sending
[] Official Elon (elonmusk, Sep 10): amplify Grok Bot draft-before-send QoL
[] Desktop: Allow once, Deny, or Always allow a matching rule
[] iPhone: Approve once or Deny
[] Auto Review: Settings → General → Auto-review
[] Require Approval beats Always Allow when both match
[] Write narrow rules, not allow everything in the browser
[] Do not approve an action you cannot identify
[] Connect only the tools the workflow needs
[] Start read-only; keep spend, send, publish, delete, and production behind approval
[] Sign out and revoke connectors when access should end
[] Deleting a Bot does not wipe shared files or browser sessions
[] Bookmark testers: delay standing inbox/CRM access until you trust the beta
[] Bookmark testers: one person burned a 7-day quota in about 8 hours
[] Testers (daveginvesting): burned a week of tokens in about 2 hours on first try
[] Testers (unicodef1wn): check Weekly usage in the account menu before any big run; one long job can eat an entire trial credit
[] Bookmark testers: SuperGrok may offer one-off usage resets in settings; use before they expire
[] Testers: gate destructive actions (delete, overwrite, irreversible send) as their own confirmation, not lumped with routine tool use
[] Testers quoting docs: Test run does real work; Stop does not unsend
[] Testers quoting Elon (cb_doge): connecting a Bot to a bank account; Elon said any loss from a bot mistake would be covered. Still keep spend behind approval
[] Official bot Link shopping: keep purchases behind approval even though the Bot can complete them on your behalf
[] Official Elon: Grok Bot buys a Tesla
[] Testers (mvanhorn): unsupervised crews claimed to multiply their own errors ~17x; draft-then-approve anything that sends; most Bots that don't own an outcome fail
[] Testers (antpalkin): end every agent's job with a hard never-without-asking list; give one Bot veto/kill power whose no beats the rest of the desk

FIRST BOTS WORTH CREATING
[] Inbox manager for email and Slack triage
[] Calendar and reservation Bot
[] Research and daily brief Bot
[] Coding Bot that can launch Cursor cloud agents
[] Testers (AlexFinn): pair a developer Bot (Cursor cloud agents + PRs) with a PM Bot on Notion/Linear that feeds tasks and grants permission — software-factory loop
[] Chief-of-staff hub that routes work to specialists
[] Personal errands Bot (tickets, food, travel, forms)
[] Content Bot that drafts in your voice for approval
[] Chief-of-staff that researches you, organizes the other Bots, and can turn the digest into a morning podcast
[] Testers (mvanhorn): Bot Advisor; own-inbox Bot; a call Bot with its own number
[] Testers (techdevnotes): default Bots circulating - Night Shift (overnight digest), Inbox Triage, Chief of Staff, Negotiator, Prototyper, Researcher, Shopper, Apartment Scout, Lookout, Competitor Watcher
[] Testers (techdevnotes): also tool-specific sales/ops/dev roles (CRM scribe, pipeline scout, ticket triager, QA, dashboard watcher)
[] Official bot + Link: Shopper Bot can now complete online purchases once link is connected (keep approval on)
[] Testers / SpaceXAI (kiaraplds): flights, tickets, groceries - delegate errands safely to your Bot
[] Testers (minchoi): one-person-company setups - money, appointments, running ops from the phone
[] Testers (niccruzpatane): Accounting Bot (invoices, spending, bills); Personal Bot (flights, rides, Airbnb, Google Calendar, Amazon orders/returns); Home Bot (lights, robots, speakers, thermostats)
[] Testers (GrokBotDev): Jess (email/calendar/Notion/Slack recap), Marketing Bot, Prospecting Sheet Builder, Reaper (kill unused subs/meetings), Human Copywriter
[] Testers (JasonL_Capital): 8 options-trading Bots (scan puts, price LEAPS, run the wheel) with copy-paste prompts
[] Testers (Michael_Fenech_): start in recruitment, e-comm, real estate, accounting, legal, SaaS, agencies, trades, founder ops

EVENTS
- Testers (cb_doge): Grok Bot Galaxy three-day event Sep 15–17 at The Howard, 661 Howard St, San Francisco (in person or livestream, 8:45am–6:00pm): create/customize Bots, teach style/goals, workflows by role, meet the team
- Testers (AsFoundX): SpaceXAI hosting Grok Bot Galaxy Sep 15–17 at The Howard, SF + worldwide livestream (persistent agents / teammate with its own computer)
